verses.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
And the earth was without form, and void (empty). And darkness was on the face of the deep (the deep waters). And the Spirit of God moved on the face of the waters.
And God said: Let there be light. And there was light.
And God saw the light, that it was good. And God divided the light from the darkness.
And God called the light Day, and the darkness God called Night. And the evening and the morning were the first day.
And God said: Let there be a firmament (sky, a wide open space) in the middle of the waters. And let the firmament (sky) divide the waters from the waters.
And God made the firmament (sky). God divided the waters which were under the firmament (sky) from the waters which were above the firmament (sky). And it was so.
And God called the firmament (sky) Heaven. And the evening and the morning were the second day.
And God said: Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together to one place. And let the dry land appear. And it was so.
And God called the dry land Earth. And the gathering together of the waters God called Seas. And God saw that it was good.
And God said: Let the earth bring out grass, the herb (plant) giving seed, and the fruit tree giving fruit after its kind, whose seed is in itself, on the earth. And it was so.
And the earth brought out grass, and herb (plant) giving seed after its kind, and the tree giving fruit, whose seed was in itself, after its kind. And God saw that it was good.
And the evening and the morning were the third day.
And God said: Let there be lights in the firmament (sky) of the heaven to divide the day from the night. And let the lights be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years.
And let the lights be in the firmament (sky) of the heaven to give light on the earth. And it was so.
And God made two great lights: the greater light (the sun) to rule the day, and the lesser light (the moon) to rule the night. God made the stars also.
And God set the lights in the firmament (sky) of the heaven to give light on the earth,
And to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was good.
And the evening and the morning were the fourth day.
And God said: Let the waters bring out many moving creatures that have life. And let fowl (birds) fly above the earth in the open firmament (sky) of heaven.

And God created great whales (great sea creatures), and every living creature that moves, which the waters brought out in great numbers, after their kind. And God created every winged fowl (birds) after its kind. And God saw that it was good.
And God blessed the creatures of the sea and the fowl (birds), saying: Be fruitful (have many young), and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas. And let the fowl (birds) multiply on the earth.
And the evening and the morning were the fifth day.
And God said: Let the earth bring out the living creature after its kind: cattle (farm animals), and creeping things, and beasts (wild animals) of the earth after their kind. And it was so.
And God made the beast of the earth after its kind, and cattle (farm animals) after their kind, and every thing that creeps on the earth after its kind. And God saw that it was good.

And God said: Let Us make man in Our image, after Our likeness. And let man have dominion (rule) over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl (birds) of the air, and over the cattle (farm animals), and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.
So God created man in His own image. In the image of God, God created him. Male and female God created them.

And God blessed the man and the woman. And God said to them: Be fruitful (have many children), and multiply, and replenish (fill) the earth, and subdue (take control of) the earth. And have dominion (rule) over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl (birds) of the air, and over every living thing that moves on the earth.
And God said: Look, I have given you every herb (plant) bearing seed, which is on the face of all the earth, and every tree which has fruit giving seed. To you it will be for meat (food).

And to every beast of the earth, and to every fowl (birds) of the air, and to every thing that creeps on the earth, which has life, I have given every green herb (plant) for meat (food). And it was so.
And God saw every thing that He had made, and look, it was very good. And the evening and the morning were the sixth day.

1.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: So the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host (everything) in them.
And on the seventh day God ended His work which He had made. And God rested on the seventh day from all His work which He had made.
And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified (set apart as holy) the seventh day. Because on that day God had rested from all His work which God created and made.
These are the generations (the history) of the heavens and of the earth when they were created, in the day that the LORD God made the earth and the heavens.

And there was every plant of the field before it was in the earth, and every herb (plant) of the field before it grew. For the LORD God had not caused it to rain on the earth. And there was not a man to till (work) the ground.
But there went up a mist from the earth, and watered the whole face of the ground.
And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground. And the LORD God breathed into the man's nostrils the breath of life. And man became a living soul (a living person).
And the LORD God planted a garden eastward in Eden. And there the LORD God put the man whom He had formed.
And out of the ground the LORD God made every tree grow that is pleasant to see, and good for food. The tree of life also was in the middle of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.
And a river went out of Eden to water the garden. And from there the river was parted, and became four heads (four rivers).
The name of the first river is Pison. That is the river which goes around the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
And the gold of that land is good. There is bdellium (a sweet-smelling gum) and the onyx stone.
And the name of the second river is Gihon. Gihon is the river that goes around the whole land of Ethiopia.
And the name of the third river is Hiddekel. Hiddekel is the river which goes toward the east of Assyria. And the fourth river is Euphrates.
And the LORD God took the man, and put the man into the garden of Eden to dress (work) the garden and to keep it.
And the LORD God commanded the man, saying: Of every tree of the garden you may freely eat.
But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, you shall not eat of it. For in the day that you eat of it you shall surely die.
And the LORD God said: It is not good that the man should be alone. I will make a help meet (a fitting helper) for the man.

And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field, and every fowl (birds) of the air. And the LORD God brought them to Adam to see what Adam would call them. And whatever Adam called every living creature, that was its name.
And Adam gave names to all cattle (farm animals), and to the fowl (birds) of the air, and to every beast of the field. But for Adam there was not found a help meet (a fitting helper) for him.
And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall on Adam, and Adam slept. And the LORD God took one of Adam's ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place.
And from the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, the LORD God made a woman. And the LORD God brought the woman to the man.
And Adam said: This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh. She shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.
So a man shall leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave (hold tight) to his wife. And the man and his wife shall be one flesh.
And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and they were not ashamed.

2.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Now the serpent (snake) was more subtle (tricky) than any beast of the field which the LORD God had made. And the serpent (snake) said to the woman: Yes, has God said: You shall not eat of every tree of the garden?
And the woman said to the serpent (snake): We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden.
But of the fruit of the tree which is in the middle of the garden, God has said: You shall not eat of it, and you shall not touch it, or you will die.
And the serpent (snake) said to the woman: You shall not surely die.
For God knows that in the day you eat of it, then your eyes shall be opened. And you shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.

And the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise. Then the woman took of its fruit, and ate. And she gave also to her husband with her, and her husband ate.
And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked. And they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons.
And they heard the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden in the cool of the day. And Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden.
And the LORD God called to Adam, and said to him: Where are you?
And Adam said: I heard Your voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked. And I hid myself.
And the LORD God said: Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten of the tree which I commanded you not to eat?
And the man said: The woman whom You gave to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I ate.
And the LORD God said to the woman: What is this that you have done? And the woman said: The serpent (snake) beguiled (tricked) me, and I ate.

And the LORD God said to the serpent (snake): Because you have done this, you are cursed above all cattle (farm animals), and above every beast of the field. On your belly you will go, and dust you will eat all the days of your life.
And I will put enmity (hate) between you and the woman, and between your seed (children) and her seed. Her seed shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise His heel.

To the woman the LORD God said: I will greatly multiply your sorrow and your conception (being pregnant). In sorrow you will bring out children. And your desire will be to your husband, and your husband will rule over you.

And to Adam the LORD God said: Because you have hearkened (listened) to the voice of your wife, and have eaten of the tree which I commanded you, saying: You shall not eat of it, the ground is cursed for your sake. In sorrow you will eat of the ground all the days of your life.
The ground will also bring out thorns and thistles to you. And you will eat the herb (plant) of the field.
In the sweat of your face you will eat bread, until you return to the ground. For out of the ground you were taken. For dust you are, and to dust you will return.
And Adam called his wife's name Eve, because she was the mother of all living.
For Adam also and for his wife the LORD God made coats of skins, and clothed them.
And the LORD God said: Look, the man has become as one of Us, to know good and evil. And now, the man might put out his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever.
So the LORD God sent the man out from the garden of Eden, to till (work) the ground from which the man was taken.

So the LORD God drove out the man. And at the east of the garden of Eden the LORD God placed Cherubims (heavenly guards), and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.

3.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V15 capitalizes His heel, because the seed of the woman points to Christ.

verses.text: And Adam knew (lay with) Eve his wife. And Eve conceived (became pregnant), and bore Cain. And Eve said: I have gotten a man from the LORD.
And Eve again bore Cain's brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller (worker) of the ground.
And in time it came to pass that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering to the LORD.
And Abel also brought of the firstlings (first-born lambs) of his flock and of their fat. And the LORD had respect (looked with favor) to Abel and to Abel's offering.
But to Cain and to Cain's offering the LORD did not have respect (look with favor). And Cain was very wroth (angry), and Cain's countenance (face) fell.
And the LORD said to Cain: Why are you wroth (very angry)? And why is your countenance (face) fallen?
If you do well, will you not be accepted? And if you do not do well, sin lies at the door. And to you shall be his desire, and you shall rule over him.
And Cain talked with Abel his brother. And it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew (killed) Abel.
And the LORD said to Cain: Where is Abel your brother? And Cain said: I do not know. Am I my brother's keeper?
And the LORD said: What have you done? The voice of your brother's blood cries to Me from the ground.
And now you are cursed from the earth, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand.
When you till (work) the ground, it will not from now on give you its strength. A fugitive and a vagabond (a wanderer with no home) you will be in the earth.
And Cain said to the LORD: My punishment is greater than I can bear.

Look, You have driven me out this day from the face of the earth. And from Your face I will be hidden. And I will be a fugitive and a vagabond (a wanderer with no home) in the earth. And it will come to pass that every one who finds me will slay (kill) me.

And the LORD said to Cain: So whoever slays (kills) Cain, vengeance (paying back) will be taken on that killer 7 times as much. And the LORD set a mark on Cain, so that no one finding Cain would kill him.
And Cain went out from the presence of the LORD, and dwelt (lived) in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.
And Cain knew (lay with) his wife, and she conceived (became pregnant), and bore Enoch. And Cain built a city, and called the name of the city after the name of his son, Enoch.
And to Enoch was born Irad. And Irad begat (became the father of) Mehujael. And Mehujael begat (became the father of) Methusael. And Methusael begat (became the father of) Lamech.
And Lamech took two wives. The name of the one was Adah, and the name of the other Zillah.
And Adah bore Jabal. Jabal was the father of those who dwell (live) in tents, and of those who have cattle (farm animals).
And Jabal's brother's name was Jubal. Jubal was the father of all those who play the harp and organ (flute).
And Zillah also bore Tubalcain, a teacher of every artificer (craftsman) in brass and iron. And the sister of Tubalcain was Naamah.
And Lamech said to his wives, Adah and Zillah: Hear my voice. You wives of Lamech, hearken (listen) to my speech. For I have slain (killed) a man for wounding me, and a young man for hurting me.
If Cain shall be avenged (paid back) 7 times, truly Lamech shall be avenged (paid back) 77 times.
And Adam knew (lay with) his wife again, and she bore a son, and called his name Seth. For Eve said: God has appointed me another seed (child) instead of Abel, whom Cain slew (killed).
And to Seth also there was born a son, and Seth called his name Enos. Then men began to call on the name of the LORD.

4.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V7 keeps the KJV's his desire and rule over him without naming who is meant, because the Hebrew leaves it open.

verses.text: This is the book of the generations (family history) of Adam. In the day that God created man, God made man in the likeness of God.
Male and female God created them. And God blessed them, and called their name Adam, in the day when they were created.
And Adam lived 130 years, and begat (became the father of) a son in his own likeness, after his image. And Adam called his name Seth.
And the days of Adam after he had begotten (become the father of) Seth were 800 years. And Adam begat (became the father of) sons and daughters.
And all the days that Adam lived were 930 years. And Adam died.
And Seth lived 105 years, and begat (became the father of) Enos.
And Seth lived after he begat (became the father of) Enos 807 years, and begat (became the father of) sons and daughters.
And all the days of Seth were 912 years. And Seth died.
And Enos lived 90 years, and begat (became the father of) Cainan.
And Enos lived after he begat (became the father of) Cainan 815 years, and begat (became the father of) sons and daughters.
And all the days of Enos were 905 years. And Enos died.
And Cainan lived 70 years, and begat (became the father of) Mahalaleel.
And Cainan lived after he begat (became the father of) Mahalaleel 840 years, and begat (became the father of) sons and daughters.
And all the days of Cainan were 910 years. And Cainan died.
And Mahalaleel lived 65 years, and begat (became the father of) Jared.
And Mahalaleel lived after he begat (became the father of) Jared 830 years, and begat (became the father of) sons and daughters.
And all the days of Mahalaleel were 895 years. And Mahalaleel died.
And Jared lived 162 years, and begat (became the father of) Enoch.
And Jared lived after he begat (became the father of) Enoch 800 years, and begat (became the father of) sons and daughters.
And all the days of Jared were 962 years. And Jared died.
And Enoch lived 65 years, and begat (became the father of) Methuselah.
And Enoch walked with God after he begat (became the father of) Methuselah 300 years, and begat (became the father of) sons and daughters.
And all the days of Enoch were 365 years.
And Enoch walked with God. And Enoch was not (was gone), for God took him.
And Methuselah lived 187 years, and begat (became the father of) Lamech.
And Methuselah lived after he begat (became the father of) Lamech 782 years, and begat (became the father of) sons and daughters.
And all the days of Methuselah were 969 years. And Methuselah died.
And Lamech lived 182 years, and begat (became the father of) a son.
And Lamech called his son's name Noah, saying: This same son will comfort us about our work and the toil (hard work) of our hands, because of the ground which the LORD has cursed.
And Lamech lived after he begat (became the father of) Noah 595 years, and begat (became the father of) sons and daughters.
And all the days of Lamech were 777 years. And Lamech died.
And Noah was 500 years old. And Noah begat (became the father of) Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

5.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born to them,
That the sons of God (angels) saw the daughters of men, that they were fair (beautiful). And the sons of God (angels) took them as wives, of all which they chose.
And the LORD said: My Spirit shall not always strive (struggle) with man, for man also is flesh. Yet man's days shall be 120 years.

There were giants in the earth in those days, and also after that. The sons of God came in to the daughters of men, and the daughters of men bore children to them. The same children became mighty men which were of old, men of renown (fame).
And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth. And God saw that every imagination of the thoughts of man's heart was only evil continually (all the time).
And it repented the LORD (the LORD was sorry) that He had made man on the earth, and it grieved the LORD at His heart.

And the LORD said: I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth: both man, and beast, and the creeping thing, and the fowls (birds) of the air. For it repents Me (I am sorry) that I have made them.
But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD.
These are the generations (family history) of Noah. Noah was a just man (a good and fair man) and perfect (blameless) in his generations (among the people of his time), and Noah walked with God.
And Noah begat (became the father of) 3 sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
The earth also was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.
And God looked on the earth, and look, it was corrupt. For all flesh (all people) had corrupted their way on the earth.
And God said to Noah: The end of all flesh is come before Me. For the earth is filled with violence through them. And look, I will destroy them with the earth.
Make for yourself an ark (big boat) of gopher wood. You shall make rooms in the ark (big boat), and shall pitch (seal) it inside and outside with pitch (tar).

And this is the fashion (way) which you shall make it: the length of the ark (big boat) shall be 300 cubits (about 450 feet), the breadth (width) of it 50 cubits (about 75 feet), and the height of it 30 cubits (about 45 feet).

A window you shall make to the ark (big boat), and you shall finish it within a cubit (about 18 inches) of the top. And the door of the ark (big boat) you shall set in its side. With lower, second, and third stories (floors) you shall make it.
And look, I, even I, bring a flood of waters on the earth, to destroy all flesh which has the breath of life, from under heaven. And every thing that is in the earth shall die.
But with you I will establish My agreement. And you shall come into the ark (big boat): you, and your sons, and your wife, and your sons' wives with you.
And of every living thing of all flesh, 2 of every sort you shall bring into the ark (big boat), to keep them alive with you. They shall be male and female.
Of fowls (birds) after their kind, and of cattle (farm animals) after their kind, of every creeping thing of the earth after its kind, 2 of every sort shall come to you, to keep them alive.
And take to yourself of all food that is eaten, and you shall gather it to you. And it shall be food for you, and for them.
So Noah did. According to all that God commanded Noah, so Noah did.

6.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. Cubits are given a feet equivalent (1 cubit = about 18 inches).

7.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V2-3 keep the KJV's by sevens without deciding whether it means 7 animals or 7 pairs, because the Hebrew leaves it open.

verses.text: And the LORD said to Noah: Come, you and all your house (family), into the ark (big boat). For I have seen you righteous (right with God) before Me in this generation (the people living now).
Of every clean beast you shall take to you by sevens, the male and his female. And of beasts that are not clean by two, the male and his female.
Of fowls (birds) also of the air by sevens, the male and the female, to keep seed (their young) alive on the face of all the earth.
For in 7 more days I will cause it to rain on the earth 40 days and 40 nights. And every living substance (thing) that I have made I will destroy from off the face of the earth.
And Noah did according to all that the LORD commanded him.
And Noah was 600 years old when the flood of waters was on the earth.
And Noah went into the ark (big boat), and his sons, and his wife, and his sons' wives with him, because of the waters of the flood.
Of clean beasts, and of beasts that are not clean, and of fowls (birds), and of every thing that creeps on the earth,
There went in 2 and 2 to Noah into the ark (big boat), the male and the female, as God had commanded Noah.
And it came to pass after 7 days that the waters of the flood were on the earth.

In the 600th year of Noah's life, in the 2nd month, the 17th day of the month, on that same day all the fountains of the great deep (the deep waters) were broken up. And the windows of heaven were opened.
And the rain was on the earth 40 days and 40 nights.
On that very same day Noah entered into the ark (big boat), and Shem, and Ham, and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and Noah's wife, and the 3 wives of his sons with them.

They went in, and every beast after its kind, and all the cattle (farm animals) after their kind, and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth after its kind, and every fowl (birds) after its kind, every bird of every sort.
And they went in to Noah into the ark (big boat), 2 and 2 of all flesh, which has the breath of life.
And those that went in, went in male and female of all flesh, as God had commanded Noah. And the LORD shut Noah in.
And the flood was 40 days on the earth. And the waters increased, and bore up the ark (big boat), and it was lifted up above the earth.
And the waters prevailed (grew strong), and were increased greatly on the earth. And the ark (big boat) went on the face of the waters.
And the waters prevailed (grew strong) exceedingly (very much) on the earth. And all the high hills that were under the whole heaven were covered.
The waters prevailed (grew strong) 15 cubits (about 22 feet) upward, and the mountains were covered.
And all flesh died that moved on the earth, both of fowl (birds), and of cattle (farm animals), and of beast, and of every creeping thing that creeps on the earth, and every man.
All in whose nostrils was the breath of life, of all that was on the dry land, died.

And every living substance (thing) was destroyed which was on the face of the ground: both man, and cattle (farm animals), and the creeping things, and the fowl (birds) of the heaven. And they were destroyed from the earth. And only Noah remained alive, and those that were with him in the ark (big boat).
And the waters prevailed (grew strong) on the earth 150 days.

And God remembered Noah, and every living thing, and all the cattle (farm animals) that were with Noah in the ark (big boat). And God made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters asswaged (went down).
The fountains also of the deep (the deep waters) and the windows of heaven were stopped. And the rain from heaven was restrained (held back).
And the waters returned from off the earth continually (all the time). And after the end of the 150 days the waters were abated (gone down).
And the ark (big boat) rested in the 7th month, on the 17th day of the month, on the mountains of Ararat.
And the waters decreased continually (all the time) until the 10th month. In the 10th month, on the 1st day of the month, the tops of the mountains were seen.
And it came to pass at the end of 40 days that Noah opened the window of the ark (big boat) which he had made.
And Noah sent out a raven, which went out to and fro (back and forth), until the waters were dried up from off the earth.
Also Noah sent out a dove from him, to see if the waters were abated (gone down) from off the face of the ground.

But the dove found no rest for the sole of her foot, and she returned to Noah into the ark (big boat), for the waters were on the face of the whole earth. Then Noah put out his hand, and took the dove, and pulled her in to him into the ark (big boat).
And Noah stayed (waited) another 7 days. And again Noah sent out the dove out of the ark (big boat).
And the dove came in to Noah in the evening. And look, in her mouth was an olive leaf plucked off. So Noah knew that the waters were abated (gone down) from off the earth.
And Noah stayed (waited) another 7 days, and sent out the dove. And the dove did not return to him any more.

And it came to pass in the 601st year, in the 1st month, the 1st day of the month, the waters were dried up from off the earth. And Noah removed the covering of the ark (big boat), and looked. And look, the face of the ground was dry.
And in the 2nd month, on the 27th day of the month, the earth was dried.
And God spoke to Noah, saying:
Go out of the ark (big boat): you, and your wife, and your sons, and your sons' wives with you.

Bring out with you every living thing that is with you, of all flesh, both of fowl (birds), and of cattle (farm animals), and of every creeping thing that creeps on the earth. So they may breed abundantly (in great numbers) in the earth, and be fruitful (have many young), and multiply on the earth.
And Noah went out, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons' wives with him.
Every beast, every creeping thing, and every fowl (birds), and whatever creeps on the earth, after their kinds, went out of the ark (big boat).
And Noah built an altar to the LORD. And Noah took of every clean beast, and of every clean fowl (birds), and offered burnt offerings on the altar.

And the LORD smelled a sweet savour (smell). And the LORD said in His heart: I will not again curse the ground any more for man's sake, for the imagination of man's heart is evil from his youth. And I will not again smite (strike down) any more every thing living, as I have done.
While the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease (stop).

8.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them: Be fruitful (have many children), and multiply, and replenish (fill) the earth.

And the fear of you and the dread (great fear) of you shall be on every beast of the earth, and on every fowl (birds) of the air, on all that moves on the earth, and on all the fishes of the sea. Into your hand they are delivered.
Every moving thing that lives shall be meat (food) for you. Even as the green herb (plant), I have given you all things.
But flesh with its life, which is its blood, you shall not eat.

And surely your blood of your lives I will require (demand an answer for). At the hand of every beast I will require (demand an answer for) it, and at the hand of man. At the hand of every man's brother I will require (demand an answer for) the life of man.
Whoever sheds man's blood, by man shall the killer's blood be shed. For in the image of God, God made man.
And you, be fruitful (have many children), and multiply. Bring out abundantly (in great numbers) in the earth, and multiply in it.
And God spoke to Noah, and to his sons with him, saying:
And I, look, I establish My agreement with you, and with your seed (children) after you,

And with every living creature that is with you, of the fowl (birds), of the cattle (farm animals), and of every beast of the earth with you, from all that go out of the ark (big boat), to every beast of the earth.
And I will establish My agreement with you. All flesh shall not be cut off any more by the waters of a flood. And there shall not any more be a flood to destroy the earth.
And God said: This is the token (sign) of the agreement which I make between Me and you and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual (never-ending) generations (all time to come).
I set My bow (rainbow) in the cloud, and it shall be for a token (sign) of an agreement between Me and the earth.
And it shall come to pass, when I bring a cloud over the earth, that the bow (rainbow) shall be seen in the cloud.
And I will remember My agreement, which is between Me and you and every living creature of all flesh. And the waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.
And the bow (rainbow) shall be in the cloud. And I will look on it, so that I may remember the everlasting agreement between God and every living creature of all flesh that is on the earth.
And God said to Noah: This is the token (sign) of the agreement which I have established between Me and all flesh that is on the earth.
And the sons of Noah, that went out of the ark (big boat), were Shem, and Ham, and Japheth. And Ham is the father of Canaan.
These are the 3 sons of Noah. And from them the whole earth was overspread (filled with people).
And Noah began to be a husbandman (farmer), and Noah planted a vineyard (grape farm).
And Noah drank of the wine, and was drunk. And Noah was uncovered inside his tent.
And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his 2 brethren (brothers) outside.

And Shem and Japheth took a garment (clothes), and laid it on both their shoulders, and went backward, and covered the nakedness of their father. And their faces were backward, and they did not see their father's nakedness.
And Noah awoke from his wine, and knew what his younger son had done to him.
And Noah said: Cursed be Canaan. A servant of servants shall Canaan be to his brethren (brothers).
And Noah said: Blessed be the LORD God of Shem. And Canaan shall be Shem's servant.
God shall enlarge Japheth, and Japheth shall dwell (live) in the tents of Shem. And Canaan shall be his servant.
And Noah lived after the flood 350 years.
And all the days of Noah were 950 years. And Noah died.

9.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Now these are the generations (family history) of the sons of Noah: Shem, Ham, and Japheth. And to them sons were born after the flood.
The sons of Japheth: Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.
And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah.
And the sons of Javan: Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
By these the isles (coastlands) of the Gentiles (the nations) were divided in their lands, every one after his tongue (language), after their families, in their nations.
And the sons of Ham: Cush, and Mizraim, and Phut, and Canaan.
And the sons of Cush: Seba, and Havilah, and Sabtah, and Raamah, and Sabtechah. And the sons of Raamah: Sheba, and Dedan.
And Cush begat (became the father of) Nimrod. Nimrod began to be a mighty one in the earth.
Nimrod was a mighty hunter before the LORD. So it is said: Even as Nimrod the mighty hunter before the LORD.
And the beginning of Nimrod's kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
Out of that land went Asshur, and built Nineveh, and the city Rehoboth, and Calah,
And Resen between Nineveh and Calah. The same is a great city.
And Mizraim begat (became the father of) Ludim, and Anamim, and Lehabim, and Naphtuhim,
And Pathrusim, and Casluhim (out of whom came Philistim), and Caphtorim.
And Canaan begat (became the father of) Sidon his firstborn, and Heth,
And the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgasite,
And the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite,
And the Arvadite, and the Zemarite, and the Hamathite. And afterward the families of the Canaanites were spread abroad.
And the border of the Canaanites was from Sidon, as you come to Gerar, to Gaza. As you go, it was to Sodom, and Gomorrah, and Admah, and Zeboim, even to Lasha.
These are the sons of Ham, after their families, after their tongues (languages), in their countries, and in their nations.
To Shem also, the father of all the children of Eber, the brother of Japheth the elder, even to Shem children were born.
The children of Shem: Elam, and Asshur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram.
And the children of Aram: Uz, and Hul, and Gether, and Mash.
And Arphaxad begat (became the father of) Salah. And Salah begat (became the father of) Eber.
And to Eber were born 2 sons. The name of one was Peleg, for in his days the earth was divided. And his brother's name was Joktan.
And Joktan begat (became the father of) Almodad, and Sheleph, and Hazarmaveth, and Jerah,
And Hadoram, and Uzal, and Diklah,
And Obal, and Abimael, and Sheba,
And Ophir, and Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.
And their dwelling (home) was from Mesha, as you go to Sephar, a mount of the east.
These are the sons of Shem, after their families, after their tongues (languages), in their lands, after their nations.
These are the families of the sons of Noah, after their generations (family lines), in their nations. And by these the nations were divided in the earth after the flood.

10.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V5 explains Gentiles as (the nations), because there were no Jews yet. V21 keeps the KJV's the brother of Japheth the elder as written.

verses.text: And the whole earth was of one language, and of one speech.
And it came to pass, as they journeyed from the east, that they found a plain in the land of Shinar. And they dwelt (lived) there.
And they said one to another: Go to (Come), let us make brick, and burn them throughly (completely). And they had brick for stone, and slime (tar) they had for mortar.
And they said: Go to (Come), let us build us a city and a tower, whose top may reach to heaven. And let us make us a name, or we will be scattered abroad on the face of the whole earth.
And the LORD came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men built.
And the LORD said: Look, the people are one, and they have all one language. And this they begin to do. And now nothing will be restrained (held back) from them, which they have imagined to do.
Go to (Come), let Us go down, and there confound (mix up) their language, so that they may not understand one another's speech.
So the LORD scattered them abroad from there on the face of all the earth. And they left off (stopped) building the city.
So the name of it is called Babel, because the LORD did there confound (mix up) the language of all the earth. And from there the LORD scattered them abroad on the face of all the earth.
These are the generations (family history) of Shem. Shem was 100 years old, and begat (became the father of) Arphaxad 2 years after the flood.
And Shem lived after he begat (became the father of) Arphaxad 500 years, and begat (became the father of) sons and daughters.
And Arphaxad lived 35 years, and begat (became the father of) Salah.
And Arphaxad lived after he begat (became the father of) Salah 403 years, and begat (became the father of) sons and daughters.
And Salah lived 30 years, and begat (became the father of) Eber.
And Salah lived after he begat (became the father of) Eber 403 years, and begat (became the father of) sons and daughters.
And Eber lived 34 years, and begat (became the father of) Peleg.
And Eber lived after he begat (became the father of) Peleg 430 years, and begat (became the father of) sons and daughters.
And Peleg lived 30 years, and begat (became the father of) Reu.
And Peleg lived after he begat (became the father of) Reu 209 years, and begat (became the father of) sons and daughters.
And Reu lived 32 years, and begat (became the father of) Serug.
And Reu lived after he begat (became the father of) Serug 207 years, and begat (became the father of) sons and daughters.
And Serug lived 30 years, and begat (became the father of) Nahor.
And Serug lived after he begat (became the father of) Nahor 200 years, and begat (became the father of) sons and daughters.
And Nahor lived 29 years, and begat (became the father of) Terah.
And Nahor lived after he begat (became the father of) Terah 119 years, and begat (became the father of) sons and daughters.
And Terah lived 70 years, and begat (became the father of) Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
Now these are the generations (family history) of Terah. Terah begat (became the father of) Abram, Nahor, and Haran. And Haran begat (became the father of) Lot.
And Haran died before his father Terah in the land of his nativity (birth), in Ur of the Chaldees.
And Abram and Nahor took wives. The name of Abram's wife was Sarai. And the name of Nahor's wife was Milcah, the daughter of Haran. Haran was the father of Milcah, and the father of Iscah.
But Sarai was barren (could not have children). Sarai had no child.

And Terah took Abram his son, and Lot the son of Haran, his son's son, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, his son Abram's wife. And they went out with them from Ur of the Chaldees, to go into the land of Canaan. And they came to Haran, and dwelt (lived) there.
And the days of Terah were 205 years. And Terah died in Haran.

11.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Now the LORD had said to Abram: Get out of your country, and from your kindred (relatives), and from your father's house, to a land that I will show you.
And I will make of you a great nation. And I will bless you, and make your name great. And you shall be a blessing.
And I will bless those who bless you, and curse the one who curses you. And in you shall all families of the earth be blessed.
So Abram departed, as the LORD had spoken to him, and Lot went with him. And Abram was 75 years old when he departed out of Haran.

And Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother's son, and all their substance (goods) that they had gathered, and the souls (people) that they had gotten in Haran. And they went out to go into the land of Canaan. And into the land of Canaan they came.
And Abram passed through the land to the place of Sichem (Shechem), to the plain of Moreh. And the Canaanite was then in the land.
And the LORD appeared to Abram, and said: To your seed (children) I will give this land. And there Abram built an altar to the LORD, who appeared to him.

And Abram removed (moved) from there to a mountain on the east of Bethel, and pitched his tent, having Bethel on the west, and Hai (Ai) on the east. And there Abram built an altar to the LORD, and called on the name of the LORD.
And Abram journeyed, going on still toward the south.
And there was a famine (time of no food) in the land. And Abram went down into Egypt to sojourn (live for a while) there, for the famine was grievous (very bad) in the land.
And it came to pass, when Abram had come near to enter into Egypt, that Abram said to Sarai his wife: Look now, I know that you are a fair (beautiful) woman to look on.
So it shall come to pass, when the Egyptians shall see you, that they shall say: This is his wife. And they will kill me, but they will save you alive.
Say, I pray you, that you are my sister, so that it may be well with me for your sake. And my soul (life) shall live because of you.
And it came to pass that, when Abram had come into Egypt, the Egyptians beheld (saw) the woman, that she was very fair (beautiful).
The princes of Pharaoh also saw Sarai, and commended (praised) her before Pharaoh. And the woman was taken into Pharaoh's house.
And Pharaoh entreated (treated) Abram well for Sarai's sake. And Abram had sheep, and oxen, and he asses (male donkeys), and menservants, and maidservants, and she asses (female donkeys), and camels.
And the LORD plagued (struck) Pharaoh and his house with great plagues (sicknesses) because of Sarai, Abram's wife.
And Pharaoh called Abram and said: What is this that you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that she was your wife?
Why did you say: She is my sister? So I might have taken her to me as a wife. Now then, look, here is your wife. Take her, and go your way.
And Pharaoh commanded his men about Abram. And they sent Abram away, and his wife, and all that he had.

12.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. Sichem and Hai keep the KJV spelling with the familiar names (Shechem, Ai) in parentheses.

verses.text: And Abram went up out of Egypt into the south: Abram, and his wife, and all that he had, and Lot with him.
And Abram was very rich in cattle (farm animals), in silver, and in gold.
And Abram went on his journeys from the south even to Bethel, to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Bethel and Hai (Ai),
To the place of the altar, which Abram had made there at the first. And there Abram called on the name of the LORD.
And Lot also, who went with Abram, had flocks, and herds, and tents.
And the land was not able to bear them, so that they might dwell (live) together. For their substance (goods) was great, so that they could not dwell (live) together.

And there was a strife (fighting) between the herdmen (herders) of Abram's cattle (farm animals) and the herdmen (herders) of Lot's cattle (farm animals). And the Canaanite and the Perizzite dwelt (lived) then in the land.
And Abram said to Lot: Let there be no strife (fighting), I pray you, between me and you, and between my herdmen (herders) and your herdmen (herders), for we are brethren (family).
Is not the whole land before you? Separate yourself, I pray you, from me. If you will take the left hand, then I will go to the right. Or if you depart to the right hand, then I will go to the left.

And Lot lifted up his eyes, and beheld (saw) all the plain of Jordan, that it was well watered everywhere, as you come to Zoar. This was before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah. The plain was even as the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt.
Then Lot chose for himself all the plain of Jordan. And Lot journeyed east. And they separated themselves the one from the other.
Abram dwelt (lived) in the land of Canaan, and Lot dwelt (lived) in the cities of the plain, and pitched his tent toward Sodom.
But the men of Sodom were wicked and sinners before the LORD exceedingly (very much).
And the LORD said to Abram, after Lot was separated from him: Lift up now your eyes, and look from the place where you are, northward, and southward, and eastward, and westward.
For all the land which you see, to you I will give it, and to your seed (children) forever.
And I will make your seed (children) as the dust of the earth. So if a man can number (count) the dust of the earth, then your seed (children) shall also be numbered (counted).
Arise, walk through the land in its length and in its breadth (width), for I will give it to you.
Then Abram removed (moved) his tent, and came and dwelt (lived) in the plain of Mamre, which is in Hebron, and built there an altar to the LORD.

13.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. Hai keeps the KJV spelling with the familiar name (Ai) in parentheses.

verses.text: And it came to pass in the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of nations,
That these kings made war with Bera king of Sodom, and with Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, and Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, which is Zoar.
All these were joined together in the vale (valley) of Siddim, which is the salt sea.
For 12 years they served Chedorlaomer, and in the 13th year they rebelled.
And in the 14th year came Chedorlaomer, and the kings that were with him, and smote (struck down) the Rephaims in Ashteroth Karnaim, and the Zuzims in Ham, and the Emims in Shaveh Kiriathaim,
And the Horites in their mount Seir, to Elparan, which is by the wilderness (desert).
And they returned, and came to Enmishpat, which is Kadesh, and smote (struck down) all the country of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites, that dwelt (lived) in Hazezontamar.

And there went out the king of Sodom, and the king of Gomorrah, and the king of Admah, and the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (the same is Zoar). And they joined battle with them in the vale (valley) of Siddim:
With Chedorlaomer the king of Elam, and with Tidal king of nations, and Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar: 4 kings with 5.
And the vale (valley) of Siddim was full of slimepits (tar pits). And the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, and fell there. And those that remained fled to the mountain.
And the 4 kings took all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah, and all their victuals (food), and went their way.
And they took Lot, Abram's brother's son, who dwelt (lived) in Sodom, and Lot's goods, and departed.

And there came one that had escaped, and told Abram the Hebrew. For Abram dwelt (lived) in the plain of Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eshcol, and brother of Aner. And these were confederate (joined in agreement) with Abram.
And when Abram heard that his brother (relative) was taken captive (prisoner), Abram armed his trained servants, born in his own house, 318 men, and pursued them to Dan.
And Abram divided himself against them, he and his servants, by night, and smote (struck down) them, and pursued them to Hobah, which is on the left hand of Damascus.
And Abram brought back all the goods, and also brought again his brother (relative) Lot, and Lot's goods, and the women also, and the people.
And the king of Sodom went out to meet Abram after his return from the slaughter of Chedorlaomer, and of the kings that were with him, at the valley of Shaveh, which is the king's dale (valley).
And Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine. And Melchizedek was the priest of the Most High God.
And Melchizedek blessed Abram, and said: Blessed be Abram of the Most High God, possessor (owner) of heaven and earth.
And blessed be the Most High God, which has delivered your enemies into your hand. And Abram gave Melchizedek tithes (a tenth part) of all.
And the king of Sodom said to Abram: Give me the persons (people), and take the goods to yourself.
And Abram said to the king of Sodom: I have lifted up my hand to the LORD, the Most High God, the possessor (owner) of heaven and earth,
That I will not take from a thread even to a shoelatchet (sandal strap), and that I will not take any thing that is yours, or else you would say: I have made Abram rich.
Except only that which the young men have eaten, and the portion (share) of the men which went with me: Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. Let them take their portion (share).

14.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V10 keeps the KJV's fell there without adding who fell. V14 and v16 keep his brother for Lot, explained as (relative), because Lot was Abram's nephew.

verses.text: After these things the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision, saying: Fear not, Abram. I am your shield, and your exceeding (very) great reward.
And Abram said: Lord GOD, what will You give me, since I go childless, and the steward (manager) of my house is this Eliezer of Damascus?
And Abram said: Look, to me You have given no seed (child). And look, one born in my house is my heir (the one who will own it all).

And look, the word of the LORD came to Abram, saying: This man shall not be your heir (the one who will own it all). But the one that shall come out of your own bowels (your own body) shall be your heir (the one who will own it all).
And the LORD brought Abram outside, and said: Look now toward heaven, and tell (count) the stars, if you are able to number (count) them. And the LORD said to Abram: So shall your seed (children) be.
And Abram believed in the LORD. And the LORD counted it to Abram for righteousness (being right with God).
And the LORD said to Abram: I am the LORD that brought you out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give you this land to inherit it.
And Abram said: Lord GOD, by what shall I know that I shall inherit it?
And the LORD said to Abram: Take Me a heifer (young cow) 3 years old, and a she goat 3 years old, and a ram 3 years old, and a turtledove (dove), and a young pigeon.
And Abram took to him all these, and divided them in the middle, and laid each piece one across from another. But the birds he did not divide.
And when the fowls (birds) came down on the carcases (dead bodies), Abram drove them away.
And when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell on Abram. And look, a horror (great fear) of great darkness fell on him.

And the LORD said to Abram: Know of a surety (for sure) that your seed (children) shall be a stranger (foreigner) in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them. And they shall afflict (make to suffer) them 400 years.
And also that nation, whom they shall serve, I will judge. And afterward they shall come out with great substance (goods).
And you shall go to your fathers in peace. You shall be buried in a good old age.
But in the 4th generation they shall come here again. For the iniquity (sin) of the Amorites is not yet full.
And it came to pass that, when the sun went down, and it was dark, look, a smoking furnace (fire pot), and a burning lamp (torch) passed between those pieces.
In the same day the LORD made an agreement with Abram, saying: To your seed (children) I have given this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates:
The Kenites, and the Kenizzites, and the Kadmonites,
And the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the Rephaims,
And the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.

15.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V4 explains bowels as (your own body), which is what the Hebrew means here.

verses.text: Now Sarai, Abram's wife, bore him no children. And Sarai had a handmaid (servant girl), an Egyptian, whose name was Hagar.

And Sarai said to Abram: Look now, the LORD has restrained (kept) me from bearing children. I pray you, go in to (lie with) my maid. It may be that I may obtain children by her. And Abram hearkened (listened) to the voice of Sarai.
And Sarai, Abram's wife, took Hagar her maid the Egyptian, after Abram had dwelt (lived) 10 years in the land of Canaan. And Sarai gave Hagar to her husband Abram to be his wife.

And Abram went in to (lay with) Hagar, and she conceived (became pregnant). And when Hagar saw that she had conceived (become pregnant), her mistress (the woman over her) was despised (looked down on) in her eyes.

And Sarai said to Abram: My wrong be on you. I have given my maid into your bosom (arms). And when she saw that she had conceived (become pregnant), I was despised (looked down on) in her eyes. The LORD judge between me and you.
But Abram said to Sarai: Look, your maid is in your hand. Do to her as it pleases you. And when Sarai dealt hardly (harshly) with Hagar, Hagar fled from her face.
And the angel of the LORD found Hagar by a fountain (spring) of water in the wilderness (desert), by the fountain in the way to Shur.
And the angel of the LORD said: Hagar, Sarai's maid, where did you come from? And where will you go? And Hagar said: I flee from the face of my mistress Sarai.
And the angel of the LORD said to her: Return to your mistress, and submit (put) yourself under her hands.
And the angel of the LORD said to her: I will multiply your seed (children) exceedingly (very much), so that it shall not be numbered (counted) for multitude (because there are so many).
And the angel of the LORD said to her: Look, you are with child (pregnant), and shall bear a son, and shall call his name Ishmael, because the LORD has heard your affliction (suffering).
And Ishmael will be a wild man. His hand will be against every man, and every man's hand against him. And Ishmael shall dwell (live) in the presence of all his brethren (brothers).
And Hagar called the name of the LORD that spoke to her: You God see me. For Hagar said: Have I also here looked after Him that sees me?
So the well was called Beerlahairoi (the well of the Living One who sees me). Look, it is between Kadesh and Bered.
And Hagar bore Abram a son. And Abram called his son's name, which Hagar bore, Ishmael.
And Abram was 86 years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram.

16.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: And when Abram was 99 years old, the LORD appeared to Abram, and said to him: I am the Almighty God. Walk before Me, and be perfect (blameless).
And I will make My agreement between Me and you, and will multiply you exceedingly (very much).
And Abram fell on his face. And God talked with him, saying:
As for Me, look, My agreement is with you, and you shall be a father of many nations.
Your name shall not any more be called Abram, but your name shall be Abraham. For a father of many nations I have made you.
And I will make you exceedingly (very much) fruitful (have many children), and I will make nations of you, and kings shall come out of you.

And I will establish My agreement between Me and you and your seed (children) after you in their generations (family lines), for an everlasting agreement, to be a God to you, and to your seed (children) after you.
And I will give to you, and to your seed (children) after you, the land in which you are a stranger (foreigner), all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession. And I will be their God.
And God said to Abraham: You shall keep My agreement then, you, and your seed (children) after you in their generations (family lines).
This is My agreement, which you shall keep, between Me and you and your seed (children) after you: every man child among you shall be circumcised (foreskin cut off).
And you shall circumcise (cut) the flesh of your foreskin. And it shall be a token (sign) of the agreement between Me and you.

And he that is 8 days old shall be circumcised (foreskin cut off) among you, every man child in your generations (family lines): he that is born in the house, or bought with money from any stranger (foreigner), which is not of your seed (children).
He that is born in your house, and he that is bought with your money, must be circumcised (foreskin cut off). And My agreement shall be in your flesh for an everlasting agreement.
And the uncircumcised (foreskin not cut off) man child whose flesh of his foreskin is not circumcised (cut), that soul (person) shall be cut off from his people. He has broken My agreement.
And God said to Abraham: As for Sarai your wife, you shall not call her name Sarai, but Sarah shall her name be.
And I will bless her, and give you a son also of her. Yes, I will bless her, and she shall be a mother of nations. Kings of people shall be of her.
Then Abraham fell on his face, and laughed, and said in his heart: Shall a child be born to him that is 100 years old? And shall Sarah, that is 90 years old, bear?
And Abraham said to God: O that Ishmael might live before You.

And God said: Sarah your wife shall bear you a son indeed (truly). And you shall call his name Isaac. And I will establish My agreement with Isaac for an everlasting agreement, and with his seed (children) after him.

And as for Ishmael, I have heard you. Look, I have blessed Ishmael, and will make him fruitful (have many children), and will multiply him exceedingly (very much). Ishmael shall beget (become the father of) 12 princes, and I will make him a great nation.
But My agreement I will establish with Isaac, which Sarah shall bear to you at this set time in the next year.
And God left off (stopped) talking with Abraham, and God went up from Abraham.

And Abraham took Ishmael his son, and all that were born in his house, and all that were bought with his money, every male among the men of Abraham's house. And Abraham circumcised (cut) the flesh of their foreskin in that very same day, as God had said to him.
And Abraham was 99 years old when he was circumcised (cut) in the flesh of his foreskin.
And Ishmael his son was 13 years old when he was circumcised (cut) in the flesh of his foreskin.
In that very same day Abraham was circumcised (foreskin cut off), and Ishmael his son.
And all the men of Abraham's house, born in the house, and bought with money from the stranger (foreigner), were circumcised (foreskin cut off) with him.

17.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: And the LORD appeared to Abraham in the plains of Mamre. And Abraham sat in the tent door in the heat of the day.
And Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked, and look, 3 men stood by him. And when Abraham saw them, he ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed himself toward the ground,
And said: My Lord, if now I have found favour (kindness) in Your sight, do not pass away, I pray You, from Your servant.
Let a little water, I pray you, be fetched (brought), and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree.
And I will fetch a morsel (piece) of bread, and comfort your hearts. After that you shall pass on, for that is why you have come to your servant. And the men said: Do so, as you have said.
And Abraham hastened (hurried) into the tent to Sarah, and said: Make ready quickly 3 measures of fine meal (flour). Knead it, and make cakes on the hearth (fireplace).
And Abraham ran to the herd, and fetched a calf tender and good, and gave it to a young man. And the young man hurried to dress (cook) it.
And Abraham took butter, and milk, and the calf which he had dressed, and set it before the men. And Abraham stood by them under the tree, and they ate.
And the men said to Abraham: Where is Sarah your wife? And Abraham said: Look, in the tent.

And the LORD said: I will certainly return to you according to the time of life (at this time next year). And look, Sarah your wife shall have a son. And Sarah heard it in the tent door, which was behind him.
Now Abraham and Sarah were old and well stricken (far along) in age. And it ceased to be with Sarah after the manner of women (Sarah was past the age to have children).
So Sarah laughed within herself, saying: After I have waxed (grown) old, shall I have pleasure, my lord being old also?
And the LORD said to Abraham: Why did Sarah laugh, saying: Shall I of a surety (for sure) bear a child, when I am old?
Is any thing too hard for the LORD? At the time appointed I will return to you, according to the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son.
Then Sarah denied, saying: I did not laugh. For she was afraid. And the LORD said: No, but you did laugh.
And the men rose up from there, and looked toward Sodom. And Abraham went with them to bring them on the way.
And the LORD said: Shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I do,
Since Abraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him?

For I know Abraham, that he will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the LORD, to do justice and judgment (what is right). So the LORD may bring on Abraham that which He has spoken of him.
And the LORD said: Because the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and because their sin is very grievous (very bad),
I will go down now, and see whether they have done altogether according to the cry of it, which has come to Me. And if not, I will know.
And the men turned their faces from there, and went toward Sodom. But Abraham stood yet before the LORD.
And Abraham drew near, and said: Will You also destroy the righteous (people right with God) with the wicked?
Peradventure (maybe) there are 50 righteous (people right with God) within the city. Will You also destroy and not spare the place for the 50 righteous (people right with God) that are in it?

That be far from You to do after this manner, to slay (kill) the righteous (people right with God) with the wicked, so that the righteous (people right with God) should be as the wicked. That be far from You. Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?
And the LORD said: If I find in Sodom 50 righteous (people right with God) within the city, then I will spare all the place for their sakes.
And Abraham answered and said: Look now, I have taken on me to speak to the Lord, though I am but dust and ashes.
Peradventure (maybe) there shall lack 5 of the 50 righteous (people right with God). Will You destroy all the city for lack of 5? And the LORD said: If I find there 45, I will not destroy it.
And Abraham spoke to Him yet again, and said: Peradventure (maybe) there shall be 40 found there. And the LORD said: I will not do it for 40's sake.
And Abraham said to Him: Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak. Peradventure (maybe) there shall 30 be found there. And the LORD said: I will not do it, if I find 30 there.
And Abraham said: Look now, I have taken on me to speak to the Lord. Peradventure (maybe) there shall be 20 found there. And the LORD said: I will not destroy it for 20's sake.
And Abraham said: Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak yet but this once. Peradventure (maybe) 10 shall be found there. And the LORD said: I will not destroy it for 10's sake.
And the LORD went His way, as soon as He had left communing (talking) with Abraham. And Abraham returned to his place.

18.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V3 keeps the KJV's My Lord (capital L) where Abraham speaks to the LORD; v12 keeps my lord (small l) for Sarah's husband.

verses.text: And there came 2 angels to Sodom at even (evening). And Lot sat in the gate of Sodom. And Lot, seeing them, rose up to meet them. And Lot bowed himself with his face toward the ground.

And Lot said: Look now, my lords, turn in, I pray you, into your servant's house, and tarry (stay) all night, and wash your feet. And you shall rise up early, and go on your ways. And the angels said: No, but we will abide (stay) in the street all night.
And Lot pressed on them greatly. And they turned in to him, and entered into his house. And Lot made them a feast, and baked unleavened bread (bread made without yeast), and they ate.
But before they lay down, the men of the city, even the men of Sodom, compassed (surrounded) the house around, both old and young, all the people from every quarter (part of the city).
And they called to Lot, and said to him: Where are the men which came in to you this night? Bring them out to us, so that we may know (lie with) them.
And Lot went out at the door to them, and shut the door after him,
And said: I pray you, brethren (brothers), do not do so wickedly.

Look now, I have 2 daughters which have not known (lain with) a man. Let me, I pray you, bring them out to you, and do to them as is good in your eyes. Only to these men do nothing, for that is why they came under the shadow of my roof.

And the men of Sodom said: Stand back. And they said again: This one fellow came in to sojourn (live for a while), and he will needs be a judge. Now we will deal worse with you than with them. And they pressed sore (hard) on the man, even Lot, and came near to break the door.
But the angels put out their hand, and pulled Lot into the house to them, and shut the door.
And the angels smote (struck down) the men that were at the door of the house with blindness, both small and great. So the men wearied (wore out) themselves to find the door.
And the angels said to Lot: Have you here any others? Son-in-law, and your sons, and your daughters, and whatever you have in the city, bring them out of this place.
For we will destroy this place, because the cry of them has waxen (grown) great before the face of the LORD. And the LORD has sent us to destroy it.

And Lot went out, and spoke to his sons-in-law, which married his daughters, and said: Up, get out of this place, for the LORD will destroy this city. But Lot seemed as one that mocked (joked) to his sons-in-law.

And when the morning arose, then the angels hastened (hurried) Lot, saying: Arise, take your wife, and your 2 daughters, which are here, or you will be consumed (destroyed) in the iniquity (sin) of the city.

And while Lot lingered (was slow to go), the men laid hold on his hand, and on the hand of his wife, and on the hand of his 2 daughters, the LORD being merciful to Lot. And they brought Lot out, and set him outside the city.

And it came to pass, when they had brought them out, that the angel said: Escape for your life. Do not look behind you, and do not stay in all the plain. Escape to the mountain, or you will be consumed (destroyed).
And Lot said to them: Oh, not so, my Lord.

Look now, Your servant has found grace in Your sight, and You have magnified (made great) Your mercy, which You have shown to me in saving my life. And I cannot escape to the mountain, or some evil will take me, and I die.
Look now, this city is near to flee to, and it is a little one. Oh, let me escape there (is it not a little one?), and my soul (life) shall live.
And the angel said to Lot: See, I have accepted you about this thing also, that I will not overthrow this city, for which you have spoken.
Hurry, escape there, for I cannot do any thing until you have come there. So the name of the city was called Zoar.
The sun had risen on the earth when Lot entered into Zoar.
Then the LORD rained on Sodom and on Gomorrah brimstone (burning sulfur) and fire from the LORD out of heaven.
And the LORD overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants (people who lived there) of the cities, and that which grew on the ground.
But Lot's wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
And Abraham got up early in the morning to the place where he stood before the LORD.
And Abraham looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah, and toward all the land of the plain, and beheld (saw), and look, the smoke of the country went up as the smoke of a furnace.

And it came to pass, when God destroyed the cities of the plain, that God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the middle of the overthrow, when God overthrew the cities in which Lot dwelt (lived).
And Lot went up out of Zoar, and dwelt (lived) in the mountain, and his 2 daughters with him, for Lot feared to dwell (live) in Zoar. And Lot dwelt (lived) in a cave, he and his 2 daughters.
And the firstborn said to the younger: Our father is old, and there is not a man in the earth to come in to (lie with) us after the manner of all the earth.
Come, let us make our father drink wine, and we will lie with him, so that we may preserve (keep alive) seed (a family line) of our father.
And they made their father drink wine that night. And the firstborn went in, and lay with her father. And Lot perceived (knew) not when she lay down, nor when she arose.

And it came to pass on the next day, that the firstborn said to the younger: Look, I lay last night with my father. Let us make him drink wine this night also. And you go in, and lie with him, so that we may preserve seed (a family line) of our father.
And they made their father drink wine that night also. And the younger arose, and lay with him. And Lot perceived (knew) not when she lay down, nor when she arose.
So both the daughters of Lot were with child (pregnant) by their father.
And the firstborn bore a son, and called his name Moab. The same is the father of the Moabites to this day.
And the younger, she also bore a son, and called his name Benammi. The same is the father of the children of Ammon to this day.

19.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. Hard chapter: v5 and v8 use the KJV's know and known, explained as (lie with) and (lain with), the same as knew (lay with) in Genesis 4:1. V17 and v21 say the angel where the KJV says he. V18 keeps the KJV's my Lord.

verses.text: And Abraham journeyed from there toward the south country, and dwelt (lived) between Kadesh and Shur, and sojourned (lived for a while) in Gerar.
And Abraham said of Sarah his wife: She is my sister. And Abimelech king of Gerar sent, and took Sarah.
But God came to Abimelech in a dream by night, and said to him: Look, you are but a dead man, because of the woman which you have taken, for she is a man's wife.
But Abimelech had not come near her. And Abimelech said: Lord, will You slay (kill) also a righteous (innocent) nation?
Did Abraham not say to me: She is my sister? And she, even she herself said: He is my brother. In the integrity (honesty) of my heart and innocency (innocence) of my hands I have done this.

And God said to Abimelech in a dream: Yes, I know that you did this in the integrity (honesty) of your heart. For I also withheld (held back) you from sinning against Me. So I did not suffer (allow) you to touch her.

Now then, restore (give back) to the man his wife, for he is a prophet, and he shall pray for you, and you shall live. And if you do not restore her, know that you shall surely die, you, and all that are yours.
So Abimelech rose early in the morning, and called all his servants, and told all these things in their ears. And the men were sore (very) afraid.

Then Abimelech called Abraham, and said to him: What have you done to us? And how have I offended you, that you have brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin? You have done deeds to me that ought not to be done.
And Abimelech said to Abraham: What did you see, that you have done this thing?
And Abraham said: Because I thought: Surely the fear of God is not in this place, and they will slay (kill) me for my wife's sake.
And yet indeed she is my sister. She is the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother. And she became my wife.

And it came to pass, when God caused me to wander from my father's house, that I said to her: This is your kindness which you shall show to me: at every place where we shall come, say of me: He is my brother.
And Abimelech took sheep, and oxen, and menservants, and womenservants, and gave them to Abraham, and restored to him Sarah his wife.
And Abimelech said: Look, my land is before you. Dwell (live) where it pleases you.

And to Sarah Abimelech said: Look, I have given your brother 1,000 pieces of silver. Look, he is to you a covering of the eyes (a sign that you did no wrong), to all that are with you, and with all other people. So Sarah was reproved (set right).
So Abraham prayed to God. And God healed Abimelech, and his wife, and his maidservants, and they bore children.
For the LORD had fast closed up all the wombs of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.

20.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V4 keeps the KJV's Lord (Adonai) and explains righteous here as (innocent). V16 explains the KJV's a covering of the eyes by its meaning.

verses.text: And the LORD visited Sarah as He had said, and the LORD did to Sarah as He had spoken.
For Sarah conceived (became pregnant), and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him.
And Abraham called the name of his son that was born to him, whom Sarah bore to him, Isaac.
And Abraham circumcised (cut off the foreskin of) his son Isaac, being 8 days old, as God had commanded him.
And Abraham was 100 years old when his son Isaac was born to him.
And Sarah said: God has made me to laugh, so that all that hear will laugh with me.
And Sarah said: Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah should have given children suck (nursed babies)? For I have borne him a son in his old age.
And the child grew, and was weaned (stopped nursing). And Abraham made a great feast the same day that Isaac was weaned.
And Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, which Hagar had borne to Abraham, mocking.
So Sarah said to Abraham: Cast out this bondwoman (slave woman) and her son. For the son of this bondwoman (slave woman) shall not be heir (the one who will own it all) with my son, even with Isaac.
And the thing was very grievous (painful) in Abraham's sight because of his son.

And God said to Abraham: Let it not be grievous in your sight because of the lad (boy), and because of your bondwoman (slave woman). In all that Sarah has said to you, hearken (listen) to her voice. For in Isaac shall your seed (children) be called.
And also of the son of the bondwoman (slave woman) I will make a nation, because he is your seed (child).

And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and took bread, and a bottle of water, and gave it to Hagar, putting it on her shoulder, and gave her the child, and sent her away. And Hagar departed, and wandered in the wilderness (desert) of Beersheba.
And the water was spent (used up) in the bottle, and Hagar cast (put) the child under one of the shrubs.

And Hagar went, and sat down across from him a good way off, as it were a bowshot (as far as an arrow flies). For she said: Let me not see the death of the child. And she sat across from him, and lifted up her voice, and wept.

And God heard the voice of the lad (boy). And the angel of God called to Hagar out of heaven, and said to her: What ails (troubles) you, Hagar? Fear not, for God has heard the voice of the lad (boy) where he is.
Arise, lift up the lad (boy), and hold him in your hand, for I will make him a great nation.
And God opened Hagar's eyes, and she saw a well of water. And she went, and filled the bottle with water, and gave the lad (boy) drink.
And God was with the lad (boy). And Ishmael grew, and dwelt (lived) in the wilderness (desert), and became an archer (a man who shoots with a bow).
And Ishmael dwelt (lived) in the wilderness (desert) of Paran. And his mother took him a wife out of the land of Egypt.
And it came to pass at that time that Abimelech and Phichol the chief captain of his host (army) spoke to Abraham, saying: God is with you in all that you do.
