Now then, swear to me here by God that you will not deal falsely with me, nor with my son, nor with my son's son. But according to the kindness that I have done to you, you shall do to me, and to the land in which you have sojourned (lived for a while).
And Abraham said: I will swear.
And Abraham reproved (corrected) Abimelech because of a well of water, which Abimelech's servants had violently taken away.
And Abimelech said: I wot (know) not who has done this thing. You did not tell me, and I did not hear of it until today.
And Abraham took sheep and oxen, and gave them to Abimelech. And both of them made an agreement.
And Abraham set 7 ewe lambs (female lambs) of the flock by themselves.
And Abimelech said to Abraham: What do these 7 ewe lambs mean, which you have set by themselves?
And Abraham said: These 7 ewe lambs you shall take from my hand, so that they may be a witness to me that I have dug this well.
So Abraham called that place Beersheba (the well of the promise), because there they both swore.
So they made an agreement at Beersheba. Then Abimelech rose up, and Phichol the chief captain of his host (army), and they returned into the land of the Philistines.
And Abraham planted a grove (a group of trees) in Beersheba, and called there on the name of the LORD, the everlasting God.
And Abraham sojourned (lived for a while) in the Philistines' land many days.

21.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V33 keeps the KJV's grove (a group of trees).

verses.text: And it came to pass after these things that God did tempt (test) Abraham, and said to him: Abraham. And Abraham said: Look, here I am.
And God said: Take now your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go into the land of Moriah. And offer him there for a burnt offering on one of the mountains which I will tell you of.

And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and saddled his ass (donkey), and took 2 of his young men with him, and Isaac his son. And Abraham clave (split) the wood for the burnt offering, and rose up, and went to the place of which God had told him.
Then on the 3rd day Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw the place afar off (far away).
And Abraham said to his young men: Abide (stay) here with the ass (donkey). And I and the lad (boy) will go yonder (over there) and worship, and come again to you.
And Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering, and laid it on Isaac his son. And Abraham took the fire in his hand, and a knife. And they went both of them together.
And Isaac spoke to Abraham his father, and said: My father. And Abraham said: Here am I, my son. And Isaac said: Look, the fire and the wood. But where is the lamb for a burnt offering?
And Abraham said: My son, God will provide Himself a lamb for a burnt offering. So they went both of them together.
And they came to the place which God had told Abraham of. And Abraham built an altar there, and laid the wood in order, and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar on the wood.
And Abraham stretched out his hand, and took the knife to slay (kill) his son.
And the angel of the LORD called to Abraham out of heaven, and said: Abraham, Abraham. And Abraham said: Here am I.

And the angel of the LORD said: Do not lay your hand on the lad (boy), and do not do any thing to him. For now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld (held back) your son, your only son, from Me.

And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and look, behind him a ram caught in a thicket (bushes) by his horns. And Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering in the stead (place) of his son.
And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovahjireh (the LORD will provide). As it is said to this day: In the mount of the LORD it shall be seen.
And the angel of the LORD called to Abraham out of heaven the 2nd time,
And said: By Myself I have sworn, says the LORD, because you have done this thing, and have not withheld (held back) your son, your only son,

That in blessing I will bless you, and in multiplying I will multiply your seed (children) as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand which is on the sea shore. And your seed (children) shall possess the gate of His enemies.
And in your seed (children) shall all the nations of the earth be blessed, because you have obeyed My voice.
So Abraham returned to his young men, and they rose up and went together to Beersheba. And Abraham dwelt (lived) at Beersheba.
And it came to pass after these things that it was told Abraham, saying: Look, Milcah, she has also borne children to your brother Nahor:
Huz his firstborn, and Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of Aram,
And Chesed, and Hazo, and Pildash, and Jidlaph, and Bethuel.
And Bethuel begat (became the father of) Rebekah. These 8 Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham's brother.
And Nahor's concubine (second wife), whose name was Reumah, she bore also Tebah, and Gaham, and Thahash, and Maachah.

22.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V1 keeps the KJV's tempt, explained as (test). V8 keeps the KJV's God will provide Himself a lamb. V17 capitalizes His enemies, because the seed points to Christ (Galatians 3:16), as with Genesis 3:15.

verses.text: And Sarah was 127 years old. These were the years of the life of Sarah.
And Sarah died in Kirjatharba. The same is Hebron in the land of Canaan. And Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to weep for her.
And Abraham stood up from before his dead, and spoke to the sons of Heth, saying:
I am a stranger (foreigner) and a sojourner (one living here for a while) with you. Give me a possession of a burying place with you, so that I may bury my dead out of my sight.
And the children of Heth answered Abraham, saying to him:
Hear us, my lord. You are a mighty prince among us. In the choice of our sepulchres (tombs) bury your dead. None of us shall withhold from you his sepulchre (tomb), but that you may bury your dead.
And Abraham stood up, and bowed himself to the people of the land, even to the children of Heth.
And Abraham communed (talked) with them, saying: If it is your mind that I should bury my dead out of my sight, hear me, and intreat (ask) for me to Ephron the son of Zohar,
That Ephron may give me the cave of Machpelah, which he has, which is in the end of his field. For as much money as it is worth he shall give it to me, for a possession of a burying place among you.

And Ephron dwelt (lived) among the children of Heth. And Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the audience (hearing) of the children of Heth, even of all that went in at the gate of his city, saying:
No, my lord, hear me. The field I give you, and the cave that is in it, I give it to you. In the presence of the sons of my people I give it to you. Bury your dead.
And Abraham bowed down himself before the people of the land.

And Abraham spoke to Ephron in the audience (hearing) of the people of the land, saying: But if you will give it, I pray you, hear me. I will give you money for the field. Take it from me, and I will bury my dead there.
And Ephron answered Abraham, saying to him:
My lord, hearken (listen) to me. The land is worth 400 shekels (small weights) of silver. What is that between me and you? Bury then your dead.

And Abraham hearkened (listened) to Ephron. And Abraham weighed to Ephron the silver, which Ephron had named in the audience (hearing) of the sons of Heth, 400 shekels (small weights) of silver, current money with the merchant (money that buyers and sellers used).

And the field of Ephron, which was in Machpelah, which was before Mamre, the field, and the cave which was in it, and all the trees that were in the field, that were in all the borders around, were made sure (given for certain)
To Abraham for a possession in the presence of the children of Heth, before all that went in at the gate of his city.
And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre. The same is Hebron in the land of Canaan.
And the field, and the cave that is in it, were made sure (given for certain) to Abraham for a possession of a burying place by the sons of Heth.

23.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: And Abraham was old, and well stricken (far along) in age. And the LORD had blessed Abraham in all things.
And Abraham said to the eldest servant of his house, that ruled over all that he had: Put, I pray you, your hand under my thigh (a way of making a serious promise).
And I will make you swear by the LORD, the God of heaven, and the God of the earth, that you shall not take a wife for my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell (live).
But you shall go to my country, and to my kindred (relatives), and take a wife for my son Isaac.
And the servant said to Abraham: Peradventure (maybe) the woman will not be willing to follow me to this land. Must I then bring your son again to the land from which you came?
And Abraham said to him: Beware that you do not bring my son there again.

The LORD God of heaven, which took me from my father's house, and from the land of my kindred (relatives), and which spoke to me, and that swore to me, saying: To your seed (children) I will give this land, He shall send His angel before you. And you shall take a wife for my son from there.
And if the woman will not be willing to follow you, then you shall be clear from this my oath (promise). Only do not bring my son there again.
And the servant put his hand under the thigh (a way of making a serious promise) of Abraham his master, and swore to him about that matter.
And the servant took 10 camels of the camels of his master, and departed, for all the goods of his master were in his hand. And the servant arose, and went to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor.
And the servant made his camels to kneel down outside the city by a well of water at the time of the evening, even the time that women go out to draw water.
And the servant said: O LORD God of my master Abraham, I pray You, send me good speed (success) this day, and show kindness to my master Abraham.
Look, I stand here by the well of water. And the daughters of the men of the city come out to draw water.

And let it come to pass that the damsel (girl) to whom I shall say: Let down your pitcher (water jar), I pray you, so that I may drink, and she shall say: Drink, and I will give your camels drink also, let the same be she that You have appointed for Your servant Isaac. And by this I shall know that You have shown kindness to my master.

And it came to pass, before he had done speaking, that look, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother, with her pitcher (water jar) on her shoulder.
And the damsel (girl) was very fair (beautiful) to look on, a virgin, and no man had known (lain with) her. And she went down to the well, and filled her pitcher (water jar), and came up.
And the servant ran to meet her, and said: Let me, I pray you, drink a little water of your pitcher (water jar).
And Rebekah said: Drink, my lord. And she hurried, and let down her pitcher (water jar) on her hand, and gave him drink.
And when Rebekah had done giving him drink, she said: I will draw water for your camels also, until they have done drinking.
And Rebekah hurried, and emptied her pitcher (water jar) into the trough (water box for animals), and ran again to the well to draw water, and drew for all his camels.
And the man, wondering at her, held his peace (was quiet), to wit (to know) whether the LORD had made his journey prosperous (successful) or not.

And it came to pass, as the camels had done drinking, that the man took a golden earring of half a shekel (a small weight) weight, and 2 bracelets for her hands of 10 shekels (small weights) weight of gold,
And said: Whose daughter are you? Tell me, I pray you. Is there room in your father's house for us to lodge (stay the night) in?
And Rebekah said to him: I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, which she bore to Nahor.
Rebekah said also to him: We have both straw and provender (animal food) enough, and room to lodge in.
And the man bowed down his head, and worshipped the LORD.

And the man said: Blessed be the LORD God of my master Abraham, who has not left my master destitute (without) of His mercy and His truth. I being in the way, the LORD led me to the house of my master's brethren (relatives).
And the damsel (girl) ran, and told them of her mother's house these things.
And Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban. And Laban ran out to the man, to the well.

And it came to pass, when Laban saw the earring and bracelets on his sister's hands, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying: So the man spoke to me, that Laban came to the man. And look, the man stood by the camels at the well.
And Laban said: Come in, you blessed of the LORD. Why do you stand outside? For I have prepared the house, and room for the camels.

And the man came into the house. And Laban ungirded (unloaded) the camels, and gave straw and provender (animal food) for the camels, and water to wash the servant's feet, and the feet of the men that were with him.
And there was set meat (food) before him to eat. But the servant said: I will not eat until I have told my errand. And Laban said: Speak on.
And the servant said: I am Abraham's servant.

And the LORD has blessed my master greatly, and he has become great. And the LORD has given him flocks, and herds, and silver, and gold, and menservants, and maidservants, and camels, and asses (donkeys).
And Sarah my master's wife bore a son to my master when she was old. And to that son my master has given all that he has.
And my master made me swear, saying: You shall not take a wife for my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I dwell (live).
But you shall go to my father's house, and to my kindred (relatives), and take a wife for my son.
And I said to my master: Peradventure (maybe) the woman will not follow me.

And my master said to me: The LORD, before whom I walk, will send His angel with you, and prosper (make successful) your way. And you shall take a wife for my son of my kindred (relatives), and of my father's house.
Then you shall be clear from this my oath (promise), when you come to my kindred (relatives). And if they do not give you one, you shall be clear from my oath (promise).
And I came this day to the well, and said: O LORD God of my master Abraham, if now You do prosper (make successful) my way which I go,
Look, I stand by the well of water. And it shall come to pass that when the virgin comes out to draw water, and I say to her: Give me, I pray you, a little water of your pitcher (water jar) to drink,
And she says to me: Both drink, and I will also draw for your camels, let the same be the woman whom the LORD has appointed for my master's son.

And before I had done speaking in my heart, look, Rebekah came out with her pitcher (water jar) on her shoulder. And she went down to the well, and drew water. And I said to her: Let me drink, I pray you.
And Rebekah made haste (hurried), and let down her pitcher (water jar) from her shoulder, and said: Drink, and I will give your camels drink also. So I drank, and she made the camels drink also.

And I asked her, and said: Whose daughter are you? And she said: The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor's son, whom Milcah bore to him. And I put the earring on her face (a nose ring), and the bracelets on her hands.
And I bowed down my head, and worshipped the LORD, and blessed the LORD God of my master Abraham, which had led me in the right way to take my master's brother's daughter for his son.
And now if you will deal kindly and truly with my master, tell me. And if not, tell me, so that I may turn to the right hand, or to the left.
Then Laban and Bethuel answered and said: The thing proceeds (comes) from the LORD. We cannot speak to you bad or good.
Look, Rebekah is before you. Take her, and go, and let her be your master's son's wife, as the LORD has spoken.
And it came to pass that, when Abraham's servant heard their words, he worshipped the LORD, bowing himself to the earth.
And the servant brought out jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment (clothes), and gave them to Rebekah. He gave also to her brother and to her mother precious things.
And they ate and drank, the servant and the men that were with him, and tarried (stayed) all night. And they rose up in the morning, and the servant said: Send me away to my master.
And Rebekah's brother and her mother said: Let the damsel (girl) abide (stay) with us a few days, at the least 10. After that she shall go.
And the servant said to them: Do not hinder (hold back) me, since the LORD has prospered (made successful) my way. Send me away so that I may go to my master.
And they said: We will call the damsel (girl), and enquire (ask) at her mouth.
And they called Rebekah, and said to her: Will you go with this man? And Rebekah said: I will go.
And they sent away Rebekah their sister, and her nurse, and Abraham's servant, and his men.
And they blessed Rebekah, and said to her: You are our sister. Be the mother of thousands of millions, and let your seed (children) possess the gate of those which hate them.
And Rebekah arose, and her damsels (servant girls), and they rode on the camels, and followed the man. And the servant took Rebekah, and went his way.
And Isaac came from the way of the well Lahairoi, for Isaac dwelt (lived) in the south country.
And Isaac went out to meditate (think quietly) in the field at the eventide (evening). And Isaac lifted up his eyes, and saw, and look, the camels were coming.
And Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Isaac, she lighted off (got down from) the camel.
For Rebekah had said to the servant: What man is this that walks in the field to meet us? And the servant had said: It is my master. So Rebekah took a vail (veil), and covered herself.
And the servant told Isaac all things that he had done.
And Isaac brought Rebekah into his mother Sarah's tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife. And Isaac loved her. And Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.

24.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V2 and v9 keep the KJV's under my thigh (a way of making a serious promise). V47 keeps the KJV's earring on her face (a nose ring).

verses.text: Then again Abraham took a wife, and her name was Keturah.
And Keturah bore him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.
And Jokshan begat (became the father of) Sheba, and Dedan. And the sons of Dedan were Asshurim, and Letushim, and Leummim.
And the sons of Midian: Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abidah, and Eldaah. All these were the children of Keturah.
And Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac.
But to the sons of the concubines (second wives), which Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts, and sent them away from Isaac his son, while he yet lived, eastward, to the east country.
And these are the days of the years of Abraham's life which he lived: 175 years.
Then Abraham gave up the ghost (spirit), and died in a good old age, an old man, and full of years. And Abraham was gathered to his people.
And his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, which is before Mamre:
The field which Abraham purchased from the sons of Heth. There Abraham was buried, and Sarah his wife.
And it came to pass after the death of Abraham that God blessed his son Isaac. And Isaac dwelt (lived) by the well Lahairoi.
Now these are the generations (family history) of Ishmael, Abraham's son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's handmaid (servant girl), bore to Abraham.
And these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their generations (family lines): the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebajoth, and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,
And Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa,
Hadar, and Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their towns, and by their castles: 12 princes according to their nations.
And these are the years of the life of Ishmael: 137 years. And Ishmael gave up the ghost (spirit) and died, and was gathered to his people.
And they dwelt (lived) from Havilah to Shur, that is before Egypt, as you go toward Assyria. And Ishmael died in the presence of all his brethren (brothers).
And these are the generations (family history) of Isaac, Abraham's son. Abraham begat (became the father of) Isaac.
And Isaac was 40 years old when he took Rebekah as his wife, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Padanaram, the sister of Laban the Syrian.

And Isaac intreated (prayed to) the LORD for his wife, because she was barren (could not have children). And the LORD was intreated (moved by prayer) by him, and Rebekah his wife conceived (became pregnant).
And the children struggled together within her. And Rebekah said: If it is so, why am I like this? And she went to enquire (ask) of the LORD.

And the LORD said to her: 2 nations are in your womb, and 2 manner of people shall be separated from your bowels (body). And the one people shall be stronger than the other people. And the elder shall serve the younger.
And when her days to be delivered (give birth) were fulfilled, look, there were twins in her womb.
And the first came out red, all over like a hairy garment (clothes). And they called his name Esau.
And after that his brother came out, and his hand took hold on Esau's heel. And his name was called Jacob. And Isaac was 60 years old when Rebekah bore them.
And the boys grew. And Esau was a cunning (skillful) hunter, a man of the field. And Jacob was a plain (quiet) man, dwelling (living) in tents.
And Isaac loved Esau, because Isaac ate of Esau's venison (wild animal meat). But Rebekah loved Jacob.
And Jacob sod (cooked) pottage (stew). And Esau came from the field, and he was faint (weak with hunger).
And Esau said to Jacob: Feed me, I pray you, with that same red pottage (stew), for I am faint (weak with hunger). So his name was called Edom (red).
And Jacob said: Sell me this day your birthright (the rights of the firstborn son).
And Esau said: Look, I am at the point to die. And what profit shall this birthright (the rights of the firstborn son) do to me?
And Jacob said: Swear to me this day. And Esau swore to him. And Esau sold his birthright (the rights of the firstborn son) to Jacob.

Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage (stew) of lentiles (lentil beans). And Esau ate and drank, and rose up, and went his way. So Esau despised (looked down on) his birthright (the rights of the firstborn son).

25.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V23 explains bowels as (body), as in Genesis 15:4.

verses.text: And there was a famine (time of no food) in the land, beside the first famine (time of no food) that was in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines, to Gerar.
And the LORD appeared to Isaac, and said: Do not go down into Egypt. Dwell (live) in the land which I shall tell you of.

Sojourn (Live for a while) in this land, and I will be with you, and will bless you. For to you, and to your seed (children), I will give all these countries. And I will perform the oath (promise) which I swore to Abraham your father.

And I will make your seed (children) to multiply as the stars of heaven, and will give to your seed (children) all these countries. And in your seed (children) shall all the nations of the earth be blessed,
Because Abraham obeyed My voice, and kept My charge (what I told him to keep), My commandments, My statutes (rules), and My laws.
And Isaac dwelt (lived) in Gerar.

And the men of the place asked Isaac about his wife. And Isaac said: She is my sister. For Isaac feared to say: She is my wife. He thought: The men of the place might kill me for Rebekah, because she was fair (beautiful) to look on.
And it came to pass, when Isaac had been there a long time, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a window, and saw, and look, Isaac was sporting (showing love) with Rebekah his wife.
And Abimelech called Isaac, and said: Look, of a surety (for sure) she is your wife. And how did you say: She is my sister? And Isaac said to him: Because I said: I might die because of her.
And Abimelech said: What is this you have done to us? One of the people might lightly (easily) have lain with your wife, and you would have brought guiltiness on us.
And Abimelech charged (commanded) all his people, saying: He that touches this man or his wife shall surely be put to death.
Then Isaac sowed (planted seed) in that land, and received in the same year a hundredfold (100 times as much). And the LORD blessed Isaac.
And the man waxed (grew) great, and went forward, and grew until he became very great.
For Isaac had possession of flocks, and possession of herds, and great store (number) of servants. And the Philistines envied (were jealous of) him.
For all the wells which his father's servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines had stopped them, and filled them with earth.
And Abimelech said to Isaac: Go from us, for you are much mightier than we.
And Isaac departed from there, and pitched his tent in the valley of Gerar, and dwelt (lived) there.

And Isaac dug again the wells of water, which they had dug in the days of Abraham his father. For the Philistines had stopped them after the death of Abraham. And Isaac called their names after the names by which his father had called them.
And Isaac's servants dug in the valley, and found there a well of springing water.

And the herdmen (herders) of Gerar did strive (argue) with Isaac's herdmen (herders), saying: The water is ours. And Isaac called the name of the well Esek (arguing), because they strove (argued) with him.
And they dug another well, and strove (argued) for that also. And Isaac called the name of it Sitnah (enemy).

And Isaac removed (moved) from there, and dug another well. And for that one they did not strive (argue). And Isaac called the name of it Rehoboth (room). And he said: For now the LORD has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful (grow in number) in the land.
And Isaac went up from there to Beersheba.

And the LORD appeared to Isaac the same night, and said: I am the God of Abraham your father. Fear not, for I am with you, and will bless you, and multiply your seed (children) for My servant Abraham's sake.
And Isaac built an altar there, and called on the name of the LORD, and pitched his tent there. And there Isaac's servants dug a well.
Then Abimelech went to Isaac from Gerar, and Ahuzzath one of his friends, and Phichol the chief captain of his army.
And Isaac said to them: Why do you come to me, since you hate me, and have sent me away from you?
And they said: We saw certainly that the LORD was with you. And we said: Let there be now an oath (promise) between us, even between us and you, and let us make an agreement with you,
That you will do us no hurt, as we have not touched you, and as we have done to you nothing but good, and have sent you away in peace. You are now the blessed of the LORD.
And Isaac made them a feast, and they ate and drank.
And they rose up betimes (early) in the morning, and swore one to another. And Isaac sent them away, and they departed from him in peace.
And it came to pass the same day that Isaac's servants came, and told him about the well which they had dug, and said to him: We have found water.
And Isaac called it Shebah (promise). So the name of the city is Beersheba to this day.
And Esau was 40 years old when he took as wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite,
Which were a grief of mind (great sorrow) to Isaac and to Rebekah.

26.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. Well names are explained: Esek (arguing), Sitnah (enemy), Rehoboth (room), Shebah (promise).

verses.text: And it came to pass that when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see, Isaac called Esau his eldest son, and said to him: My son. And Esau said to him: Look, here am I.
And Isaac said: Look now, I am old. I do not know the day of my death.
Now then, take, I pray you, your weapons, your quiver (arrow holder) and your bow, and go out to the field, and take me some venison (wild animal meat).
And make me savoury meat (tasty food), such as I love, and bring it to me, so that I may eat, so that my soul may bless you before I die.
And Rebekah heard when Isaac spoke to Esau his son. And Esau went to the field to hunt for venison (wild animal meat), and to bring it.
And Rebekah spoke to Jacob her son, saying: Look, I heard your father speak to Esau your brother, saying:
Bring me venison (wild animal meat), and make me savoury meat (tasty food), so that I may eat, and bless you before the LORD before my death.
Now then, my son, obey my voice according to that which I command you.
Go now to the flock, and fetch me from there 2 good kids (young goats) of the goats. And I will make them savoury meat (tasty food) for your father, such as he loves.
And you shall bring it to your father, so that he may eat, and so that he may bless you before his death.
And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother: Look, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.
My father peradventure (maybe) will feel me, and I shall seem to him as a deceiver (liar). And I shall bring a curse on me, and not a blessing.
And his mother said to Jacob: On me be your curse, my son. Only obey my voice, and go fetch them for me.
And Jacob went, and fetched, and brought them to his mother. And his mother made savoury meat (tasty food), such as his father loved.
And Rebekah took goodly (the best) raiment (clothes) of her eldest son Esau, which were with her in the house, and put them on Jacob her younger son.
And Rebekah put the skins of the kids (young goats) of the goats on his hands, and on the smooth part of his neck.
And Rebekah gave the savoury meat (tasty food) and the bread, which she had prepared, into the hand of her son Jacob.
And Jacob came to his father, and said: My father. And Isaac said: Here am I. Who are you, my son?
And Jacob said to his father: I am Esau your firstborn. I have done as you told me. Arise, I pray you, sit and eat of my venison (wild animal meat), so that your soul may bless me.
And Isaac said to his son: How is it that you have found it so quickly, my son? And Jacob said: Because the LORD your God brought it to me.
And Isaac said to Jacob: Come near, I pray you, so that I may feel you, my son, whether you are my very son Esau or not.
And Jacob went near to Isaac his father. And Isaac felt him, and said: The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.
And Isaac discerned (knew) him not, because his hands were hairy, as his brother Esau's hands. So Isaac blessed Jacob.
And Isaac said: Are you my very son Esau? And Jacob said: I am.

And Isaac said: Bring it near to me, and I will eat of my son's venison (wild animal meat), so that my soul may bless you. And Jacob brought it near to him, and Isaac ate. And Jacob brought him wine, and Isaac drank.
And his father Isaac said to him: Come near now, and kiss me, my son.
And Jacob came near, and kissed him. And Isaac smelled the smell of his raiment (clothes), and blessed him, and said: See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the LORD has blessed.
So God give you of the dew of heaven, and the fatness (richness) of the earth, and plenty of corn (grain) and wine.

Let people serve you, and nations bow down to you. Be lord over your brethren (brothers), and let your mother's sons bow down to you. Cursed be every one that curses you, and blessed be he that blesses you.

And it came to pass, as soon as Isaac had made an end of blessing Jacob, and Jacob was yet scarce (hardly) gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother came in from his hunting.

And Esau also had made savoury meat (tasty food), and brought it to his father, and said to his father: Let my father arise, and eat of his son's venison (wild animal meat), so that your soul may bless me.
And Isaac his father said to him: Who are you? And Esau said: I am your son, your firstborn Esau.

And Isaac trembled very exceedingly (very much), and said: Who? Where is he that has taken venison (wild animal meat), and brought it to me, and I have eaten of all before you came, and have blessed him? Yes, and he shall be blessed.
And when Esau heard the words of his father, he cried with a great and exceeding (very) bitter cry, and said to his father: Bless me, even me also, O my father.
And Isaac said: Your brother came with subtilty (trickery), and has taken away your blessing.

And Esau said: Is he not rightly named Jacob? For he has supplanted (tricked me and taken my place) these 2 times. He took away my birthright (the rights of the firstborn son). And look, now he has taken away my blessing. And Esau said: Have you not reserved (kept) a blessing for me?

And Isaac answered and said to Esau: Look, I have made him your lord, and all his brethren (brothers) I have given to him for servants. And with corn (grain) and wine I have sustained (supplied) him. And what shall I do now for you, my son?
And Esau said to his father: Have you but one blessing, my father? Bless me, even me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.
And Isaac his father answered and said to him: Look, your dwelling (home) shall be the fatness (richness) of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above.
And by your sword you shall live, and shall serve your brother. And it shall come to pass when you shall have the dominion (rule), that you shall break his yoke (heavy wooden bar) from off your neck.

And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing with which his father blessed him. And Esau said in his heart: The days of mourning for my father are at hand (near). Then I will slay (kill) my brother Jacob.

And these words of Esau her elder son were told to Rebekah. And she sent and called Jacob her younger son, and said to him: Look, your brother Esau, about you, does comfort himself, purposing (planning) to kill you.
Now then, my son, obey my voice. And arise, flee to Laban my brother, to Haran.
And tarry (stay) with him a few days, until your brother's fury (great anger) turns away,

Until your brother's anger turns away from you, and he forgets that which you have done to him. Then I will send, and fetch you from there. Why should I be deprived (left without) of you both in one day?

And Rebekah said to Isaac: I am weary (tired) of my life because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob takes a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these which are of the daughters of the land, what good shall my life do me?

27.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V36 explains Jacob's name by the KJV's supplanted (tricked me and took my place). V39 follows the KJV: your dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth.

verses.text: And Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged (commanded) him, and said to him: You shall not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.
Arise, go to Padanaram, to the house of Bethuel your mother's father. And take a wife from there of the daughters of Laban your mother's brother.
And God Almighty bless you, and make you fruitful (have many children), and multiply you, so that you may be a multitude (great number) of people.
And give you the blessing of Abraham, to you, and to your seed (children) with you, so that you may inherit the land in which you are a stranger (foreigner), which God gave to Abraham.
And Isaac sent away Jacob. And Jacob went to Padanaram to Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob's and Esau's mother.

Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob, and sent him away to Padanaram, to take him a wife from there. And Esau saw that as Isaac blessed him he gave him a charge (command), saying: You shall not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.
And Esau saw that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother, and had gone to Padanaram.
And Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan did not please Isaac his father.
Then Esau went to Ishmael, and took to the wives which he had Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham's son, the sister of Nebajoth, to be his wife.
And Jacob went out from Beersheba, and went toward Haran.

And Jacob lighted (came) on a certain place, and tarried (stayed) there all night, because the sun was set. And Jacob took of the stones of that place, and put them for his pillows, and lay down in that place to sleep.
And Jacob dreamed, and look, a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven. And look, the angels of God ascending and descending (going up and coming down) on it.
And look, the LORD stood above it, and said: I am the LORD God of Abraham your father, and the God of Isaac. The land on which you lie, to you I will give it, and to your seed (children).

And your seed (children) shall be as the dust of the earth, and you shall spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south. And in you and in your seed (children) shall all the families of the earth be blessed.
And look, I am with you, and will keep you in all places where you go, and will bring you again into this land. For I will not leave you, until I have done that which I have spoken to you of.
And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said: Surely the LORD is in this place, and I did not know it.
And Jacob was afraid, and said: How dreadful (full of fear and wonder) is this place. This is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.
And Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put for his pillows, and set it up for a pillar (standing stone), and poured oil on the top of it.
And Jacob called the name of that place Bethel (house of God). But the name of that city was called Luz at the first.
And Jacob vowed a vow (made a promise to God), saying: If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment (clothes) to put on,
So that I come again to my father's house in peace, then the LORD shall be my God.
And this stone, which I have set for a pillar (standing stone), shall be God's house. And of all that You shall give me I will surely give the tenth to You.

28.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Then Jacob went on his journey, and came into the land of the people of the east.
And Jacob looked, and look, a well in the field. And look, there were 3 flocks of sheep lying by it, for out of that well they watered the flocks. And a great stone was on the well's mouth.
And there all the flocks were gathered. And they rolled the stone from the well's mouth, and watered the sheep, and put the stone again on the well's mouth in its place.
And Jacob said to them: My brethren (brothers), where are you from? And they said: We are from Haran.
And Jacob said to them: Do you know Laban the son of Nahor? And they said: We know him.
And Jacob said to them: Is he well? And they said: He is well. And look, Rachel his daughter comes with the sheep.
And Jacob said: Look, it is yet high day (the middle of the day). It is not time that the cattle (flocks) should be gathered together. Water the sheep, and go and feed them.
And they said: We cannot, until all the flocks are gathered together, and until they roll the stone from the well's mouth. Then we water the sheep.
And while Jacob yet spoke with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep, for she kept them.

And it came to pass, when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother's brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother's brother, that Jacob went near, and rolled the stone from the well's mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mother's brother.
And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and wept.
And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's brother (relative), and that he was Rebekah's son. And Rachel ran and told her father.

And it came to pass, when Laban heard the tidings (news) of Jacob his sister's son, that Laban ran to meet him, and embraced (hugged) him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. And Jacob told Laban all these things.
And Laban said to him: Surely you are my bone and my flesh. And Jacob abode (stayed) with him the space (time) of a month.
And Laban said to Jacob: Because you are my brother (relative), should you then serve me for nought (nothing)? Tell me, what shall your wages (pay) be?
And Laban had 2 daughters. The name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
Leah was tender (weak) eyed, but Rachel was beautiful and well favoured (good-looking).
And Jacob loved Rachel, and said: I will serve you 7 years for Rachel your younger daughter.
And Laban said: It is better that I give her to you than that I should give her to another man. Abide (Stay) with me.
And Jacob served 7 years for Rachel. And they seemed to him but a few days, for the love he had for her.
And Jacob said to Laban: Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, so that I may go in to (lie with) her.
And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast.
And it came to pass in the evening that Laban took Leah his daughter, and brought her to Jacob. And Jacob went in to (lay with) her.
And Laban gave to his daughter Leah Zilpah his maid (servant girl) for a handmaid (servant girl).
And it came to pass that in the morning, look, it was Leah. And Jacob said to Laban: What is this you have done to me? Did I not serve with you for Rachel? Why then have you beguiled (tricked) me?
And Laban said: It must not be so done in our country, to give the younger before the firstborn.
Fulfil her week (finish her wedding week), and we will give you this one also for the service which you shall serve with me yet 7 other years.
And Jacob did so, and fulfilled her week. And Laban gave him Rachel his daughter as wife also.
And Laban gave to Rachel his daughter Bilhah his handmaid (servant girl) to be her maid (servant girl).
And Jacob went in (lay with) Rachel also, and he loved Rachel more than Leah, and served with Laban yet 7 other years.
And when the LORD saw that Leah was hated (loved less), He opened her womb. But Rachel was barren (could not have children).
And Leah conceived (became pregnant), and bore a son, and she called his name Reuben. For she said: Surely the LORD has looked on my affliction (suffering). Now then my husband will love me.

And Leah conceived (became pregnant) again, and bore a son, and said: Because the LORD has heard that I was hated (loved less), He has therefore given me this son also. And she called his name Simeon.
And Leah conceived (became pregnant) again, and bore a son, and said: Now this time my husband will be joined to me, because I have borne him 3 sons. So his name was called Levi.
And Leah conceived (became pregnant) again, and bore a son. And she said: Now I will praise the LORD. So she called his name Judah, and left (stopped) bearing.

29.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V17 keeps the KJV's tender eyed. V31 and v33 keep the KJV's hated, explained as (loved less).

verses.text: And when Rachel saw that she bore Jacob no children, Rachel envied (was jealous of) her sister, and said to Jacob: Give me children, or else I die.
And Jacob's anger was kindled (burned) against Rachel. And he said: Am I in God's stead (place), who has withheld (held back) from you the fruit of the womb?
And Rachel said: Look, my maid (servant girl) Bilhah. Go in to (lie with) her, and she shall bear on my knees, so that I may also have children by her.
And Rachel gave him Bilhah her handmaid (servant girl) as wife. And Jacob went in to (lay with) her.
And Bilhah conceived (became pregnant), and bore Jacob a son.
And Rachel said: God has judged me, and has also heard my voice, and has given me a son. So she called his name Dan.
And Bilhah, Rachel's maid (servant girl), conceived (became pregnant) again, and bore Jacob a 2nd son.
And Rachel said: With great wrestlings I have wrestled with my sister, and I have prevailed (won). And she called his name Naphtali.
When Leah saw that she had left (stopped) bearing, she took Zilpah her maid (servant girl), and gave her to Jacob as wife.
And Zilpah, Leah's maid (servant girl), bore Jacob a son.
And Leah said: A troop (a large group) comes. And she called his name Gad.
And Zilpah, Leah's maid (servant girl), bore Jacob a 2nd son.
And Leah said: Happy am I, for the daughters will call me blessed. And she called his name Asher.

And Reuben went in the days of wheat harvest, and found mandrakes (a plant people believed helped women have children) in the field, and brought them to his mother Leah. Then Rachel said to Leah: Give me, I pray you, of your son's mandrakes.

And Leah said to her: Is it a small matter that you have taken my husband? And would you take away my son's mandrakes also? And Rachel said: So Jacob shall lie with you tonight for your son's mandrakes.

And Jacob came out of the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him, and said: You must come in to (lie with) me, for surely I have hired you with my son's mandrakes. And Jacob lay with her that night.
And God hearkened (listened) to Leah, and she conceived (became pregnant), and bore Jacob the 5th son.
And Leah said: God has given me my hire (pay), because I have given my maiden (servant girl) to my husband. And she called his name Issachar.
And Leah conceived (became pregnant) again, and bore Jacob the 6th son.
And Leah said: God has endued (given) me with a good dowry (gift). Now my husband will dwell (live) with me, because I have borne him 6 sons. And she called his name Zebulun.
And afterwards Leah bore a daughter, and called her name Dinah.
And God remembered Rachel, and God hearkened (listened) to her, and opened her womb.
And Rachel conceived (became pregnant), and bore a son, and said: God has taken away my reproach (shame).
And she called his name Joseph, and said: The LORD shall add to me another son.
And it came to pass, when Rachel had borne Joseph, that Jacob said to Laban: Send me away, so that I may go to my own place, and to my country.
Give me my wives and my children, for whom I have served you, and let me go. For you know my service which I have done for you.
And Laban said to him: I pray you, if I have found favour (kindness) in your eyes, tarry (stay). For I have learned by experience that the LORD has blessed me for your sake.
And Laban said: Appoint (name) me your wages (pay), and I will give it.
And Jacob said to him: You know how I have served you, and how your cattle (flock animals) were with me.
For it was little which you had before I came, and it is now increased to a multitude (great number). And the LORD has blessed you since my coming. And now when shall I provide for my own house also?
And Laban said: What shall I give you? And Jacob said: You shall not give me any thing. If you will do this thing for me, I will again feed and keep your flock.

I will pass through all your flock today, removing from there all the speckled (with small spots) and spotted cattle (flock animals), and all the brown cattle (flock animals) among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats. And of such shall be my hire (pay).

So my righteousness (honesty) shall answer for me in time to come, when it shall come for my hire before your face. Every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and brown among the sheep, that shall be counted stolen with me.
And Laban said: Look, I wish it might be according to your word.

And Laban removed (moved) that day the he goats that were ringstraked (striped) and spotted, and all the she goats that were speckled and spotted, and every one that had some white in it, and all the brown among the sheep, and gave them into the hand of his sons.
And Laban set 3 days' journey between himself and Jacob. And Jacob fed the rest of Laban's flocks.
And Jacob took rods (sticks) of green poplar, and of the hazel and chesnut tree, and pilled (peeled) white strakes (stripes) in them, and made the white appear which was in the rods.
And Jacob set the rods which he had pilled before the flocks in the gutters (channels) in the watering troughs when the flocks came to drink, so that they should conceive when they came to drink.
And the flocks conceived (became pregnant) before the rods, and brought out cattle (flock animals) ringstraked (striped), speckled, and spotted.

And Jacob did separate the lambs, and set the faces of the flocks toward the ringstraked, and all the brown in the flock of Laban. And Jacob put his own flocks by themselves, and did not put them with Laban's cattle (flock animals).

And it came to pass, whenever the stronger cattle (flock animals) did conceive, that Jacob laid the rods before the eyes of the cattle (flock animals) in the gutters, so that they might conceive among the rods.
But when the cattle (flock animals) were feeble (weak), Jacob did not put them in. So the feebler were Laban's, and the stronger Jacob's.
And the man increased exceedingly (very much), and had much cattle (flock animals), and maidservants, and menservants, and camels, and asses (donkeys).

30.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V14-16 keep the KJV's mandrakes (a plant people believed helped women have children).

verses.text: And Jacob heard the words of Laban's sons. Laban's sons were saying: Jacob has taken away all that was our father's. And of that which was our father's, Jacob has gotten all this glory (wealth).
And Jacob beheld (saw) the countenance (face) of Laban. And look, Laban's face was not toward Jacob as before.
And the LORD said to Jacob: Return to the land of your fathers. Return to your kindred (relatives), and I will be with you.
And Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah to the field, to his flock.
And Jacob said to Rachel and Leah: I see your father's countenance (face). Your father's face is not toward me as before. But the God of my father has been with me.
And you know that with all my power I have served your father.
And your father has deceived me, and changed my wages (pay) 10 times. But God did not suffer (allow) your father to hurt me.

If Laban said: The speckled (with small spots) shall be your wages (pay). Then all the cattle (flock animals) bore speckled (with small spots). And if Laban said: The ringstraked (striped) shall be your hire (pay). Then all the cattle (flock animals) bore ringstraked (striped).
So God has taken away the cattle (flock animals) of your father. God has given the cattle (flock animals) to me.

And it came to pass, when the cattle (flock animals) conceived (became pregnant), I lifted up my eyes. And I saw in a dream. And look, the rams which leaped on the cattle (flock animals) were ringstraked (striped), speckled (with small spots), and grisled (gray-spotted).
And the angel of God spoke to me in a dream, saying: Jacob. And I said: Here am I.

And the angel said: Lift up now your eyes, and see. All the rams which leap on the cattle (flock animals) are ringstraked (striped), speckled (with small spots), and grisled (gray-spotted). For I have seen all that Laban does to you.

I am the God of Bethel. There you anointed (poured oil on) the pillar (standing stone), and there you vowed a vow (made a promise) to Me. Now arise, get out from this land. Return to the land of your kindred (relatives).
And Rachel and Leah answered Jacob: Is there yet any portion (share) for us? Is there any inheritance for us in our father's house?
Are we not counted by our father as strangers (foreigners)? For our father has sold us, and has quite devoured (used up) our money also.
God has taken all the riches from our father. All those riches are ours, and our children's. Now then, whatever God has said to you, do.
Then Jacob rose up, and set his sons and his wives on camels.

And Jacob carried away all his cattle (flock animals), and all the goods Jacob had gotten. These were the cattle (flock animals) Jacob had gotten in Padanaram. Jacob went to go to Isaac his father in the land of Canaan.
And Laban went to shear (cut the wool of) his sheep. And Rachel had stolen the images (household idols) that were her father's.
And Jacob stole away unawares (secretly) from Laban the Syrian. Jacob did not tell Laban that Jacob fled.
So Jacob fled with all that Jacob had. And Jacob rose up, and passed over the river. And Jacob set his face (headed) toward the mount Gilead.
And it was told Laban on the 3rd day that Jacob had fled.
And Laban took his brethren (relatives), and pursued after Jacob 7 days' journey. And Laban and his brethren (relatives) overtook Jacob in the mount Gilead.
And God came to Laban the Syrian in a dream by night. God said to Laban: Take heed (be careful). Speak not to Jacob either good or bad.
Then Laban overtook Jacob. Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the mount. And Laban with his brethren (relatives) pitched in the mount of Gilead.
And Laban said to Jacob: What have you done? You have stolen away unawares (secretly) from me. You have carried away my daughters, as captives taken with the sword.

Why did you flee away secretly, and steal away from me? Why did you not tell me? Then I might have sent you away with mirth (joy) and with songs. I would have sent you away with tabret (small drum) and with harp.
And you have not suffered (allowed) me to kiss my sons (grandsons) and my daughters? You have now done foolishly in so doing.
It is in the power of my hand to do you hurt. But the God of your father spoke to me last night. God said: Take heed (be careful). Speak not to Jacob either good or bad.
And now, you would needs (had to) be gone. You sore longed (greatly wanted to go) after your father's house. Yet why have you stolen my gods (household idols)?
And Jacob answered and said to Laban: Because I was afraid. For I said: Peradventure (maybe) you would take your daughters from me by force.

Let whoever has your gods (household idols) not live. Before our brethren (relatives), discern (see) what is yours with me. Take what is yours to you. For Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen the gods (household idols).

And Laban went into Jacob's tent, and into Leah's tent. Laban went into the tents of the 2 maidservants (servant girls). But Laban did not find the images (household idols). Then Laban went out of Leah's tent, and entered into Rachel's tent.

Now Rachel had taken the images (household idols). Rachel put the images (household idols) in the camel's furniture (saddle). Rachel sat on the saddle. Laban searched all the tent, but did not find the images (household idols).

And Rachel said to her father: Let it not displease (upset) my lord. I cannot rise up before you. For the custom of women (my monthly time) is on me. And Laban searched, but did not find the images (household idols).
And Jacob was wroth (very angry), and chode (argued angrily) with Laban. And Jacob answered and said to Laban: What is my trespass (wrong)? What is my sin, that you have so hotly pursued after me?

You have searched all my stuff. What have you found of all your household stuff? Set what you found here before my brethren (relatives) and your brethren (relatives). Then the brethren (relatives) may judge between us both.
These 20 years I have been with you. Your ewes (female sheep) and your she goats have not cast (lost) any young (babies). And the rams of your flock I have not eaten.
That which was torn by beasts I did not bring to you. I bore the loss of the torn animal. From my hand you did require (demand) every loss, stolen by day or by night.
This is how I was. In the day the drought (heat) consumed (wore out) me, and the frost by night. And my sleep departed from my eyes.
So I have been 20 years in your house. I served you 14 years for your 2 daughters. And I served 6 years for your cattle (flock animals). And you have changed my wages (pay) 10 times.

The God of my father was with me. He is the God of Abraham, and the Fear of Isaac (the God Isaac feared). Without God, surely you would have sent me away now empty. God has seen my affliction (suffering) and the labor (hard work) of my hands. God rebuked (corrected) you last night.

And Laban answered and said to Jacob: These daughters are my daughters. These children are my children, and these cattle (flock animals) are my cattle (flock animals). All that you see is mine. And what can I do this day to these my daughters? What can I do to the children which my daughters have borne?
Now then come, let us make an agreement, I and you. And let the agreement be for a witness between me and you.
And Jacob took a stone, and set the stone up for a pillar (standing stone).
And Jacob said to his brethren (relatives): Gather stones. And the brethren (relatives) took stones, and made a heap. And the men ate there on the heap.
And Laban called the heap Jegarsahadutha (heap of witness). But Jacob called the heap Galeed (heap of witness).
And Laban said: This heap is a witness between me and you this day. So the name of the heap was called Galeed (heap of witness).
The heap was also called Mizpah (watchtower). For Laban said: The LORD watch between me and you, when we are apart.
Suppose you afflict (hurt) my daughters, or take other wives beside my daughters. No man is with us. See, God is witness between me and you.
And Laban said to Jacob: Look at this heap. And look at this pillar (standing stone), which I have cast between me and you.
This heap is witness, and this pillar (standing stone) is witness. I will not pass over this heap to you for harm. You shall not pass over this heap and this pillar (standing stone) to me, for harm.
The God of Abraham and the God of Nahor judge between us. This is the God of their father (Terah). And Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac (the God Isaac feared).
Then Jacob offered sacrifice on the mount, and called his brethren (relatives) to eat bread. And Jacob and his brethren (relatives) ate bread, and tarried (stayed) all night in the mount.
And early in the morning Laban rose up. Laban kissed and blessed his sons (grandsons) and his daughters. Then Laban departed and returned to Laban's own place.

31.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V19, v30, v32-35 explain the KJV's images and gods as (household idols). V42 and v53 keep the KJV's the Fear of Isaac (the God Isaac feared). Brethren is explained as (relatives); in v28 and v55 sons is explained as (grandsons).

verses.text: And Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met Jacob.
And when Jacob saw the angels, Jacob said: This is God's host (army). And Jacob called the name of that place Mahanaim (two camps).
And Jacob sent messengers ahead to Esau his brother. Jacob sent the messengers to the land of Seir, the country of Edom.
Jacob commanded the messengers: This is what you shall speak to my lord Esau. Your servant Jacob says this: I have sojourned (lived for a while) with Laban. And I have stayed there until now.
And I have oxen, and asses (donkeys), flocks, menservants, and womenservants (servant women). I have sent to tell my lord. This is so that I may find grace (favor) in your sight.
And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying: We came to your brother Esau. And also Esau comes to meet you, and 400 men with Esau.
Then Jacob was greatly afraid and troubled. Jacob divided his people, the flocks, the herds, and the camels into 2 bands (groups).
And Jacob said: If Esau comes to the one company, and smites (strikes) that company. Then the other company which is left shall escape.
Jacob said: O God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac. You are the LORD which said to me: Return to your country. Return to your kindred (relatives), and I will deal well with you.

I am not worthy of the least of all the mercies. I am not worthy of all the truth. You have shown these to Your servant. For with my staff (walking stick) I passed over this Jordan. And now I have become 2 bands (groups).

Deliver me, I pray You, from the hand of my brother. Deliver me from the hand of Esau. For I fear Esau. I fear Esau will come and smite (strike) me, and the mother with the children (the mothers and the children).
And You said: I will surely do you good. I will make your seed (children) as the sand of the sea. The sand cannot be numbered for multitude (because there is so much).
And Jacob lodged (stayed the night) there that same night. Jacob took a present for Esau his brother, from what Jacob had at hand:
200 she goats, and 20 he goats, 200 ewes (female sheep), and 20 rams,
30 milch (milk) camels with colts (young ones), 40 kine (cows), and 10 bulls. Also 20 she asses (female donkeys), and 10 foals (young donkeys).
Jacob delivered the animals into the hand of his servants, every drove (herd) by itself. And Jacob said to his servants: Pass over before me. Put a space between drove (herd) and drove (herd).
Jacob commanded the foremost (first servant). Jacob said: When Esau my brother meets you, Esau will ask: Whose are you? And where are you going? And whose are these animals before you?
Then you shall say: The animals are your servant Jacob's. The animals are a present sent to my lord Esau. And look, also Jacob is behind us.
So Jacob commanded the 2nd, and the 3rd, and all that followed the droves (herds). Jacob said: In this manner you shall speak to Esau, when you find Esau.

And say also: Look, your servant Jacob is behind us. For Jacob said: I will appease (calm) Esau with the present that goes before me. And afterward I will see Esau's face. Peradventure (maybe) Esau will accept me.
So the present went over before Jacob. And Jacob himself lodged (stayed the night) that night in the company (camp).
Jacob rose up that night, and took his 2 wives, and his 2 womenservants (servant women). Jacob also took his 11 sons, and passed over the ford (shallow crossing) Jabbok.
And Jacob took his family, and sent his family over the brook. And Jacob sent over all that Jacob had.
And Jacob was left alone. And a man wrestled with Jacob until the breaking of the day.

And the man did not prevail (win) against Jacob. When the man saw this, the man touched the hollow of Jacob's thigh (hip socket). The hollow of Jacob's thigh (hip socket) was out of joint (pulled out of place). This happened as the man wrestled with Jacob.
And the man said: Let me go, for the day breaks. And Jacob said: I will not let you go, except (unless) you bless me.
And the man said to Jacob: What is your name? And Jacob said: Jacob.
And the man said: Your name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel. For as a prince you have power with God and with men. And you have prevailed (won).
And Jacob asked the man, and said: Tell me, I pray you, your name. And the man said: Why is it that you ask after my name? And the man blessed Jacob there.
And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel (the face of God). For Jacob said: I have seen God face to face. And my life is preserved (kept safe).
And as Jacob passed over Penuel (the face of God), the sun rose on Jacob. And Jacob halted (limped) on his thigh.

To this day, the children of Israel do not eat the sinew (cord of muscle) that shrank. That sinew (cord of muscle) is on the hollow of the thigh (hip socket). For the man touched the hollow of Jacob's thigh (hip socket) in the sinew (cord of muscle) that shrank.

32.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. Revised 2026-11-23 for the 14-word sentence rule and Deaf-first names in place of pronouns. V24-29 call the one who wrestled the man, as the KJV does; in v30 Jacob says he has seen God face to face. V7 uses troubled for the KJV's distressed (house rule). V25 and v32 explain the hollow of the thigh as (hip socket); v31 Penuel is the same place as Peniel.

verses.text: And Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked. And look, Esau came, and 400 men with Esau. Jacob divided the children to Leah, and to Rachel, and to the 2 handmaids (servant girls).
And Jacob put the handmaids (servant girls) and the handmaids' children foremost (in front). Leah and her children came after. Rachel and Joseph came hindermost (at the back).
And Jacob passed over before his family. Jacob bowed himself to the ground 7 times, until Jacob came near to Esau.
And Esau ran to meet Jacob, and embraced (hugged) Jacob. Esau fell on Jacob's neck, and kissed Jacob. And Jacob and Esau wept.
And Esau lifted up his eyes, and saw the women and the children. Esau said: Who are those with you? And Jacob said: The children which God has graciously given your servant.
Then the handmaidens (servant girls) came near, with the handmaidens' children. And the handmaidens and the children bowed themselves.
And Leah also came near with her children. Leah and her children bowed themselves. And after came Joseph near, and Rachel. Joseph and Rachel bowed themselves.
And Esau said: What do you mean by all this drove (herd) which I met? Jacob said: These animals are to find grace (favor) in the sight of my lord.
And Esau said: I have enough, my brother. Keep what you have for yourself.
And Jacob said: No, I pray you. If I have found grace (favor) in your sight, receive my present at my hand. I have seen your face, as though I had seen the face of God. And you were pleased with me.
Take, I pray you, my blessing that is brought to you. For God has dealt graciously (kindly) with me. And I have enough. And Jacob urged (pressed) Esau, and Esau took the present.
And Esau said: Let us take our journey, and let us go. And I will go before you.

And Jacob said to Esau: My lord knows that the children are tender (young and weak). And the flocks and herds with young (nursing babies) are with me. If men should overdrive (push too hard) the animals one day, all the flock will die.

Let my lord, I pray you, pass over before his servant. And I will lead on softly (slowly). I will go as the cattle (farm animals) before me and the children can endure. I will go on until I come to my lord in Seir.
Esau said: Let me now leave with you some of the folk (people) with me. And Jacob said: What need is there? Let me find grace (favor) in the sight of my lord.
So Esau returned that day on his way to Seir.
And Jacob journeyed to Succoth (booths), and built a house for himself. Jacob made booths (shelters) for his cattle (farm animals). So the name of the place is called Succoth (booths).
And Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem, in the land of Canaan. Jacob had come from Padanaram. And Jacob pitched his tent before the city.
And Jacob bought a parcel (piece) of a field, where Jacob had spread his tent. Jacob bought the parcel from the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem's father. Jacob paid 100 pieces of money.
And Jacob erected (set up) an altar there, and called the altar Elelohe-Israel (God, the God of Israel).

33.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. Revised 2026-11-23 for the 14-word sentence rule and Deaf-first names in place of pronouns. V18 follows the KJV: Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem. V13 with young means nursing animals. V20 uses the KJV spelling Elelohe-Israel.

verses.text: And Dinah went out to see the daughters of the land. Dinah was the daughter Leah bore to Jacob.
And Shechem was the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country. When Shechem saw Dinah, Shechem took Dinah. Shechem lay with Dinah, and defiled (shamed) Dinah.
And Shechem's soul clave (held tight) to Dinah the daughter of Jacob. And Shechem loved the damsel (girl), and spoke kindly to the damsel (girl).
And Shechem spoke to his father Hamor, saying: Get me this damsel (girl) as wife.

And Jacob heard that Shechem had defiled (shamed) Dinah his daughter. Now Jacob's sons were with Jacob's cattle (farm animals) in the field. And Jacob held his peace (was quiet) until Jacob's sons had come.
And Hamor the father of Shechem went out to Jacob to commune (talk) with Jacob.

And the sons of Jacob heard what happened, and came out of the field. And the men were grieved (hurt), and the men were very wroth (angry). For Shechem had wrought (done) folly (a shameful thing) in Israel by lying with Jacob's daughter. This thing ought not to be done.
And Hamor communed (talked) with Jacob and his sons. Hamor said: The soul of my son Shechem longs for your daughter. I pray you, give Dinah to Shechem as wife.
And make marriages with us. Give your daughters to us, and take our daughters to you.
And you shall dwell (live) with us, and the land shall be before you. Dwell (live) and trade in the land, and get possessions in the land.
And Shechem spoke to Dinah's father and to Dinah's brethren (brothers). Shechem said: Let me find grace (favor) in your eyes. And what you shall say to me I will give.
Ask me ever so much dowry (bride price) and gift. And I will give as you shall say to me. But give me the damsel (girl) as wife.
And the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father deceitfully (with lies). For Shechem had defiled (shamed) Dinah, the sister of Jacob's sons.
And Jacob's sons said to Shechem and Hamor: We cannot do this thing. We cannot give our sister to one that is uncircumcised (foreskin not cut off). For that would be a reproach (shame) to us.
But in this we will consent (agree) to you. If you will be as we are, every male of you must be circumcised (foreskin cut off).
Then we will give our daughters to you. And we will take your daughters to us. And we will dwell (live) with you, and we will become one people.
But if you will not hearken (listen) to us to be circumcised (foreskin cut off). Then we will take our daughter, and we will be gone.
And the words of Jacob's sons pleased Hamor, and Shechem, Hamor's son.
And the young man deferred (delayed) not to do the thing. For Shechem had delight in Jacob's daughter. And Shechem was more honorable (respected) than all the house of his father.
And Hamor and Shechem his son came to the gate of their city. Hamor and Shechem communed (talked) with the men of their city, saying:

These men are peaceable with us. So let these men dwell (live) and trade in the land. For look, the land is large enough for these men. Let us take daughters from these men for wives. And let us give our daughters to these men.
Every male among us must be circumcised (foreskin cut off), as these men are circumcised (foreskin cut off). Only then will the men consent (agree) to dwell (live) with us as one people.
Shall not the cattle (farm animals), substance (goods), and every beast of these men be ours? Only let us consent (agree) to these men, and these men will dwell (live) with us.
All that went out of the city gate hearkened (listened) to Hamor and Shechem. And every male was circumcised (foreskin cut off), all that went out of the city gate.

On the 3rd day, the men of the city were sore (in pain). Simeon and Levi, 2 of Jacob's sons and Dinah's brethren (brothers), each took his sword. Simeon and Levi came on the city boldly, and slew (killed) all the males.
Simeon and Levi slew (killed) Hamor and Shechem with the edge of the sword. Then Simeon and Levi took Dinah out of Shechem's house, and went out.
The sons of Jacob came on the slain (dead), and spoiled (robbed) the city. This was because the city had defiled (shamed) Dinah, the sister of Jacob's sons.
Jacob's sons took the city's sheep, and oxen, and asses (donkeys). Jacob's sons took what was in the city, and what was in the field,
And all the city's wealth. And all the little ones (children) and wives of the city, Jacob's sons took captive. And Jacob's sons spoiled (robbed) even all that was in the house.

And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi: You have troubled me. You have made me to stink (be hated) among the inhabitants (people) of the land. I stink among the Canaanites and the Perizzites. And I am few in number. The Canaanites and Perizzites shall gather themselves together against me, and slay (kill) me. And I shall be destroyed, I and my house (family).
Simeon and Levi said: Should Shechem deal with our sister as with a harlot (prostitute)?

34.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. Revised 2026-11-23 for the 14-word sentence rule and Deaf-first names in place of pronouns. Hard chapter: v2 keeps the KJV's lay with, and defiled (shamed). V31 keeps the KJV's harlot (prostitute). In v27 the KJV's they had defiled means the city.

verses.text: And God said to Jacob: Arise, go up to Bethel, and dwell (live) there. And make an altar there to God, who appeared to you. God appeared to you when you fled from the face of Esau your brother.
Then Jacob spoke to his household, and to all that were with Jacob. Jacob said: Put away the strange (foreign) gods that are among you. And be clean, and change your garments (clothes).
And let us arise, and go up to Bethel. And I will make an altar there to God. God answered me in the day of my trouble. And God was with me in the way which I went.

And the people gave Jacob all the strange (foreign) gods which the people had. The people also gave Jacob all the earrings in the people's ears. And Jacob hid the gods and earrings under the oak which was by Shechem.
And Jacob's family journeyed. And the terror of God was on the cities around Jacob's family. And the people of those cities did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.
So Jacob came to Luz, in the land of Canaan. Luz is Bethel. Jacob came with all the people that were with Jacob.
And Jacob built an altar there, and called the place Elbethel (the God of Bethel). For God appeared to Jacob there, when Jacob fled from the face of Esau.
But Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died. Deborah was buried below Bethel under an oak. And the name of the oak was called Allonbachuth (oak of weeping).
And God appeared to Jacob again, when Jacob came out of Padanaram. And God blessed Jacob.
And God said to Jacob: Your name is Jacob. Your name shall not be called any more Jacob. But Israel shall be your name. And God called Jacob's name Israel.
And God said to Jacob: I am God Almighty. Be fruitful (have many children) and multiply. A nation and a company of nations shall be of you. And kings shall come out of your loins (body).
And the land which I gave Abraham and Isaac, I will give to you. And to your seed (children) after you I will give the land.
And God went up from Jacob in the place where God talked with Jacob.
And Jacob set up a pillar (standing stone) where God talked with Jacob. The pillar was of stone. And Jacob poured a drink offering on the pillar. And Jacob poured oil on the pillar.
And Jacob called the place Bethel (house of God). There God spoke with Jacob.
And Jacob's family journeyed from Bethel. And there was but a little way to come to Ephrath. And Rachel travailed (was in labor to give birth), and Rachel had hard labor.
And when Rachel was in hard labor, the midwife (woman who helps at a birth) said to Rachel: Fear not. You shall have this son also.

Rachel's soul was in departing (Rachel was dying), for Rachel died. Then Rachel called the son's name Benoni (son of my sorrow). But the son's father, Jacob, called the son Benjamin (son of my right hand).
And Rachel died, and was buried in the way to Ephrath. Ephrath is Bethlehem.
And Jacob set a pillar (standing stone) on Rachel's grave. That is the pillar (standing stone) of Rachel's grave to this day.
And Israel (Jacob) journeyed, and spread his tent beyond the tower of Edar.

When Israel (Jacob) dwelt (lived) in that land, Reuben went and lay with Bilhah. Bilhah was Reuben's father's concubine (second wife). And Israel (Jacob) heard what Reuben did. Now the sons of Jacob were 12:
The sons of Leah: Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
The sons of Rachel: Joseph, and Benjamin.
And the sons of Bilhah, Rachel's handmaid (servant girl): Dan, and Naphtali.
And the sons of Zilpah, Leah's handmaid (servant girl): Gad, and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob, which were born to Jacob in Padanaram.
And Jacob came to Isaac his father to Mamre, to the city of Arbah. Arbah is Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac sojourned (lived for a while).
And the days of Isaac were 180 years.
And Isaac gave up the ghost (spirit), and died, and was gathered to his people. Isaac was old and full of days. And Isaac's sons Esau and Jacob buried Isaac.
