verses.text: Now these are the generations (family history) of Esau, who is Edom.
Esau took his wives of the daughters of Canaan. Esau took Adah the daughter of Elon the Hittite. Esau took Aholibamah the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite.
And Esau took Bashemath, Ishmael's daughter, sister of Nebajoth.
And Adah bore Eliphaz to Esau. And Bashemath bore Reuel.
And Aholibamah bore Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah. These are the sons of Esau, born to Esau in the land of Canaan.

Esau took his wives, sons, daughters, and all the persons of his house. Esau also took his cattle (farm animals), all his beasts, and all his substance (goods). Esau had gotten these in the land of Canaan. And Esau went into the country away from the face of his brother Jacob.

For Esau and Jacob had too many riches to dwell (live) together. The land where Esau and Jacob were strangers (foreigners) could not bear (support) both. This was because of the cattle (farm animals) of Esau and Jacob.
So Esau dwelt (lived) in mount Seir. Esau is Edom.
These are the generations (family history) of Esau the father of the Edomites in mount Seir.
These are the names of Esau's sons. Eliphaz was the son of Adah, the wife of Esau. Reuel was the son of Bashemath, the wife of Esau.
And the sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Gatam, and Kenaz.
And Timna was concubine (second wife) to Eliphaz, Esau's son. And Timna bore Amalek to Eliphaz. These were the sons of Adah, Esau's wife.
And these are the sons of Reuel: Nahath, and Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These were the sons of Bashemath, Esau's wife.
And these were the sons of Aholibamah, Esau's wife. Aholibamah was the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon. And Aholibamah bore Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah to Esau.
These were dukes (chiefs) of the sons of Esau. The sons of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn son, were these dukes (chiefs). Duke (chief) Teman, duke (chief) Omar, duke (chief) Zepho, duke (chief) Kenaz,
Duke (chief) Korah, duke (chief) Gatam, duke (chief) Amalek. These are the dukes (chiefs) that came of Eliphaz in the land of Edom. These were the sons of Adah.

And these are the sons of Reuel, Esau's son. Duke (chief) Nahath, duke (chief) Zerah, duke (chief) Shammah, duke (chief) Mizzah. These are the dukes (chiefs) that came of Reuel in the land of Edom. These are the sons of Bashemath, Esau's wife.

And these are the sons of Aholibamah, Esau's wife. Duke (chief) Jeush, duke (chief) Jaalam, duke (chief) Korah. These were the dukes (chiefs) that came of Aholibamah the daughter of Anah, Esau's wife.
These are the sons of Esau, who is Edom. And these are the dukes (chiefs) of Esau's sons.
These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who inhabited (lived in) the land. The sons were Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah,
And Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan. These are the dukes (chiefs) of the Horites, Seir's children, in the land of Edom.
And the children of Lotan were Hori and Hemam. And Lotan's sister was Timna.
And the children of Shobal were these: Alvan, and Manahath, and Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
And these are the children of Zibeon: both Ajah, and Anah. This was that Anah that found the mules in the wilderness (desert), as he fed the asses (donkeys) of Zibeon his father.
And the children of Anah were these: Dishon, and Aholibamah the daughter of Anah.
And these are the children of Dishon: Hemdan, and Eshban, and Ithran, and Cheran.
The children of Ezer are these: Bilhan, and Zaavan, and Akan.
The children of Dishan are these: Uz, and Aran.
These are the dukes (chiefs) that came of the Horites: duke (chief) Lotan, duke (chief) Shobal, duke (chief) Zibeon, duke (chief) Anah,
Duke (Chief) Dishon, duke (chief) Ezer, duke (chief) Dishan. These are the dukes (chiefs) that came of Hori, among their dukes (chiefs) in the land of Seir.
And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Israel.
And Bela the son of Beor reigned in Edom. And the name of his city was Dinhabah.
And Bela died, and Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his stead (place).
And Jobab died, and Husham of the land of Temani reigned in his stead (place).
And Husham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad, who smote (struck down) Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his stead (place). And the name of his city was Avith.
And Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his stead (place).
And Samlah died, and Saul of Rehoboth by the river reigned in his stead (place).
And Saul died, and Baalhanan the son of Achbor reigned in his stead (place).
And Baalhanan the son of Achbor died, and Hadar reigned in his stead (place). And the name of his city was Pau. And his wife's name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.
And these are the names of the dukes (chiefs) that came of Esau, according to their families, after their places, by their names: duke (chief) Timnah, duke (chief) Alvah, duke (chief) Jetheth,
Duke (Chief) Aholibamah, duke (chief) Elah, duke (chief) Pinon,
Duke (Chief) Kenaz, duke (chief) Teman, duke (chief) Mibzar,
Duke (Chief) Magdiel, duke (chief) Iram. These are the dukes (chiefs) of Edom, according to their habitations (homes) in the land of their possession. He is Esau the father of the Edomites.

36.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. verses.text: And Jacob dwelt (lived) in the land in which his father was a stranger (foreigner), in the land of Canaan.

These are the generations (family history) of Jacob. Joseph, being 17 years old, was feeding the flock with his brethren (brothers). And the lad (boy) was with the sons of Bilhah, and with the sons of Zilpah, his father's wives. And Joseph brought to his father their evil report.
Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because Joseph was the son of his old age. And Israel made him a coat of many colours.
And when his brethren (brothers) saw that their father loved Joseph more than all his brethren (brothers), they hated him, and could not speak peaceably to him.
And Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it to his brethren (brothers). And they hated him yet the more.
And Joseph said to them: Hear, I pray you, this dream which I have dreamed.
For look, we were binding sheaves (bundles of grain) in the field. And look, my sheaf arose, and also stood upright. And look, your sheaves stood around, and made obeisance (bowed down) to my sheaf.
And his brethren (brothers) said to him: Shall you indeed reign over us? Or shall you indeed have dominion (rule) over us? And they hated him yet the more for his dreams, and for his words.

And Joseph dreamed yet another dream, and told it to his brethren (brothers), and said: Look, I have dreamed a dream more. And look, the sun and the moon and the 11 stars made obeisance (bowed down) to me.

And Joseph told it to his father, and to his brethren (brothers). And his father rebuked (scolded) him, and said to him: What is this dream that you have dreamed? Shall I and your mother and your brethren (brothers) indeed come to bow down ourselves to you to the earth?
And his brethren (brothers) envied (were jealous of) him. But his father observed the saying (kept it in mind).
And his brethren (brothers) went to feed their father's flock in Shechem.
And Israel said to Joseph: Do not your brethren (brothers) feed the flock in Shechem? Come, and I will send you to them. And Joseph said to him: Here am I.

And Israel said to him: Go, I pray you, see whether it is well with your brethren (brothers), and well with the flocks, and bring me word again. So Israel sent him out of the vale (valley) of Hebron, and Joseph came to Shechem.
And a certain man found Joseph, and look, he was wandering in the field. And the man asked him, saying: What are you looking for?
And Joseph said: I am looking for my brethren (brothers). Tell me, I pray you, where they feed their flocks.
And the man said: They have departed from here, for I heard them say: Let us go to Dothan. And Joseph went after his brethren (brothers), and found them in Dothan.
And when they saw him afar off (far away), even before he came near to them, they conspired (made a secret plan) against him to slay (kill) him.
And they said one to another: Look, this dreamer comes.
Come now then, and let us slay (kill) him, and cast him into some pit, and we will say: Some evil beast has devoured (eaten) him. And we shall see what will become of his dreams.
And Reuben heard it, and he delivered him out of their hands, and said: Let us not kill him.

And Reuben said to them: Shed no blood, but cast him into this pit that is in the wilderness (desert), and lay no hand on him. Reuben said this so that he might rid him out of their hands, to deliver him to his father again.
And it came to pass, when Joseph had come to his brethren (brothers), that they stript (pulled) Joseph out of his coat, his coat of many colours that was on him.
And they took Joseph, and cast him into a pit. And the pit was empty. There was no water in it.

And they sat down to eat bread. And they lifted up their eyes and looked, and look, a company of Ishmeelites came from Gilead with their camels carrying spicery (spices) and balm (healing oil) and myrrh (sweet-smelling gum), going to carry it down to Egypt.
And Judah said to his brethren (brothers): What profit is it if we slay (kill) our brother, and conceal (hide) his blood?
Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites, and let not our hand be on him, for he is our brother and our flesh. And his brethren (brothers) were content (agreed).

Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen (traders). And they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for 20 pieces of silver. And they brought Joseph into Egypt.
And Reuben returned to the pit. And look, Joseph was not in the pit. And Reuben rent (tore) his clothes.
And Reuben returned to his brethren (brothers), and said: The child is not (is gone). And I, where shall I go?
And they took Joseph's coat, and killed a kid (young goat) of the goats, and dipped the coat in the blood.
And they sent the coat of many colours, and they brought it to their father, and said: This we have found. Know now whether it is your son's coat or not.
And Jacob knew it, and said: It is my son's coat. An evil beast has devoured (eaten) him. Joseph is without doubt rent (torn) in pieces.
And Jacob rent (tore) his clothes, and put sackcloth (rough cloth worn when sorry) on his loins (waist), and mourned for his son many days.
And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him. But he refused to be comforted, and he said: For I will go down into the grave to my son mourning. So his father wept for him.
And the Midianites sold Joseph into Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh's, and captain of the guard.

37.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. verses.text: And it came to pass at that time that Judah went down from his brethren (brothers), and turned in to a certain Adullamite, whose name was Hirah.
And Judah saw there a daughter of a certain Canaanite, whose name was Shuah. And Judah took her, and went in to (lay with) her.
And she conceived (became pregnant), and bore a son. And Judah called his name Er.
And she conceived (became pregnant) again, and bore a son. And she called his name Onan.
And she yet again conceived (became pregnant), and bore a son, and called his name Shelah. And Judah was at Chezib when she bore him.
And Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, whose name was Tamar.
And Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the LORD. And the LORD slew (killed) him.
And Judah said to Onan: Go in to (lie with) your brother's wife, and marry her, and raise up seed (have a child) for your brother.

And Onan knew that the seed (child) would not be his. And it came to pass, when he went in to (lay with) his brother's wife, that he spilled it (his seed) on the ground, so that he would not give seed (a child) to his brother.
And the thing which Onan did displeased the LORD. So the LORD slew (killed) him also.

Then Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law: Remain a widow at your father's house, until Shelah my son is grown. For Judah said: Peradventure (maybe) he might die also, as his brethren (brothers) did. And Tamar went and dwelt (lived) in her father's house.
And in time the daughter of Shuah, Judah's wife, died. And Judah was comforted, and went up to his sheepshearers (men who cut the wool of sheep) to Timnath, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite.
And it was told Tamar, saying: Look, your father-in-law goes up to Timnath to shear (cut the wool of) his sheep.

And Tamar put her widow's garments (clothes) off from her, and covered herself with a vail (veil), and wrapped herself, and sat in an open place, which is by the way to Timnath. For she saw that Shelah was grown, and she was not given to him as wife.
When Judah saw her, he thought her to be a harlot (prostitute), because she had covered her face.

And Judah turned to her by the way, and said: Come, I pray you, let me come in to (lie with) you. For he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said: What will you give me, so that you may come in to (lie with) me?
And Judah said: I will send you a kid (young goat) from the flock. And she said: Will you give me a pledge (something to hold as a promise), until you send it?

And Judah said: What pledge shall I give you? And she said: Your signet (seal ring), and your bracelets, and your staff that is in your hand. And Judah gave them to her, and came in to (lay with) her, and she conceived (became pregnant) by him.
And Tamar arose, and went away, and laid her vail (veil) by from her, and put on the garments (clothes) of her widowhood.
And Judah sent the kid (young goat) by the hand of his friend the Adullamite, to receive his pledge from the woman's hand. But he did not find her.
Then Hirah asked the men of that place, saying: Where is the harlot (prostitute), that was openly by the way side? And they said: There was no harlot (prostitute) in this place.
And Hirah returned to Judah, and said: I cannot find her. And also the men of the place said that there was no harlot (prostitute) in this place.
And Judah said: Let her take it to her, or we will be shamed. Look, I sent this kid (young goat), and you have not found her.

And it came to pass about 3 months after, that it was told Judah, saying: Tamar your daughter-in-law has played the harlot (prostitute). And also, look, she is with child by whoredom (sexual sin). And Judah said: Bring her out, and let her be burnt.

When she was brought out, she sent to her father-in-law, saying: By the man whose these are, I am with child. And she said: Discern (look and know), I pray you, whose are these, the signet (seal ring), and bracelets, and staff.
And Judah acknowledged them, and said: She has been more righteous (right) than I, because I did not give her to Shelah my son. And Judah knew (lay with) her again no more.
And it came to pass in the time of her travail (giving birth) that, look, twins were in her womb.

And it came to pass, when she travailed (was giving birth), that the one put out his hand. And the midwife (woman who helps at a birth) took and bound on his hand a scarlet (bright red) thread, saying: This came out first.

And it came to pass, as he drew back his hand, that look, his brother came out. And she said: How have you broken out? This breach (breaking out) be on you. So his name was called Pharez (breaking out).
And afterward his brother came out, that had the scarlet (bright red) thread on his hand. And his name was called Zarah.

verses.text: And Joseph was brought down to Egypt. And Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him from the hands of the Ishmeelites, which had brought him down there.
And the LORD was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous (successful) man. And he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.
And his master saw that the LORD was with Joseph, and that the LORD made all that Joseph did to prosper (succeed) in his hand.
And Joseph found grace in his master's sight, and he served him. And Potiphar made him overseer (manager) over his house, and all that he had he put into Joseph's hand.

And it came to pass from the time that Potiphar had made Joseph overseer (manager) in his house, and over all that he had, that the LORD blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake. And the blessing of the LORD was on all that Potiphar had in the house, and in the field.
And Potiphar left all that he had in Joseph's hand. And Potiphar knew not ought (anything) he had, except the bread which he ate. And Joseph was a goodly person, and well favoured (good-looking).
And it came to pass after these things that his master's wife cast her eyes on Joseph. And she said: Lie with me.
But Joseph refused, and said to his master's wife: Look, my master wots (knows) not what is with me in the house, and he has committed (given) all that he has to my hand.
There is none greater in this house than I. And he has not kept back any thing from me but you, because you are his wife. How then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?
And it came to pass, as she spoke to Joseph day by day, that he hearkened (listened) not to her, to lie by her, or to be with her.
And it came to pass about this time that Joseph went into the house to do his business. And there was none of the men of the house there inside.
And she caught him by his garment (clothes), saying: Lie with me. And Joseph left his garment (clothes) in her hand, and fled, and got out.
And it came to pass, when she saw that he had left his garment (clothes) in her hand, and had fled out,
That she called to the men of her house, and spoke to them, saying: See, he has brought in a Hebrew to us to mock us. He came in to me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice.
And it came to pass, when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment (clothes) with me, and fled, and got out.
And she laid up his garment (clothes) by her, until his lord came home.
And she spoke to Potiphar with these words, saying: The Hebrew servant, which you have brought to us, came in to me to mock me.
And it came to pass, as I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment (clothes) with me, and fled out.
And it came to pass, when his master heard the words of his wife, which she spoke to him, saying: This is what your servant did to me, that his wrath (anger) was kindled (burned).
And Joseph's master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king's prisoners were bound. And Joseph was there in the prison.
But the LORD was with Joseph, and showed him mercy, and gave him favour (kindness) in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
And the keeper of the prison committed (gave) to Joseph's hand all the prisoners that were in the prison. And whatever they did there, Joseph was the doer of it.
The keeper of the prison did not look to any thing that was under Joseph's hand, because the LORD was with Joseph. And that which he did, the LORD made it to prosper (succeed).

39.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V7, v12 and v14 keep the KJV's own words, lie with me. Kept hidden (needs-review) until the editor reviews it.

verses.text: And it came to pass after these things that the butler (cupbearer) of the king of Egypt and his baker had offended their lord the king of Egypt.
And Pharaoh was wroth (very angry) against 2 of his officers, against the chief of the butlers (cupbearers), and against the chief of the bakers.
And Pharaoh put them in ward (under guard) in the house of the captain of the guard, into the prison, the place where Joseph was bound.
And the captain of the guard charged (put) Joseph with them, and he served them. And they continued a season (a time) in ward (under guard).

And they dreamed a dream, both of them, each man his dream in one night, each man according to the interpretation (meaning) of his dream, the butler (cupbearer) and the baker of the king of Egypt, which were bound in the prison.
And Joseph came in to them in the morning, and looked on them, and look, they were sad.
And Joseph asked Pharaoh's officers that were with him in the ward (guard house) of his lord's house, saying: Why do you look so sad today?

And they said to him: We have dreamed a dream, and there is no interpreter (one who tells the meaning) of it. And Joseph said to them: Do not interpretations (meanings) belong to God? Tell me them, I pray you.
And the chief butler (cupbearer) told his dream to Joseph, and said to him: In my dream, look, a vine was before me.
And in the vine were 3 branches. And it was as though it budded, and her blossoms shot out, and the clusters of it brought out ripe grapes.
And Pharaoh's cup was in my hand. And I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh's cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh's hand.
And Joseph said to him: This is the interpretation (meaning) of it: the 3 branches are 3 days.

Yet within 3 days Pharaoh shall lift up your head (call you back to honor), and restore you to your place. And you shall deliver Pharaoh's cup into his hand, after the former manner when you were his butler (cupbearer).
But think on me when it shall be well with you, and show kindness, I pray you, to me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house.
For indeed I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews. And here also I have done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.
When the chief baker saw that the interpretation (meaning) was good, he said to Joseph: I also was in my dream, and look, I had 3 white baskets on my head.
And in the uppermost basket there were all kinds of bakemeats (baked foods) for Pharaoh. And the birds ate them out of the basket on my head.
And Joseph answered and said: This is the interpretation (meaning) of it: the 3 baskets are 3 days.
Yet within 3 days Pharaoh shall lift up your head from off you (cut off your head), and shall hang you on a tree. And the birds shall eat your flesh from off you.

And it came to pass the 3rd day, which was Pharaoh's birthday, that he made a feast for all his servants. And he lifted up the head (brought out) of the chief butler (cupbearer) and of the chief baker among his servants.
And Pharaoh restored the chief butler (cupbearer) to his butlership (job) again. And the chief butler (cupbearer) gave the cup into Pharaoh's hand.
But Pharaoh hanged the chief baker, as Joseph had interpreted (told the meaning) to them.
Yet the chief butler (cupbearer) did not remember Joseph, but forgat (forgot) him.

40.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V13 and v19-20 keep the KJV's lift up your head, explained by its meaning in each verse. V16 keeps the KJV's 3 white baskets. Kept hidden (needs-review) until the editor reviews it.

verses.text: And it came to pass at the end of 2 full years that Pharaoh dreamed. And look, he stood by the river.
And look, there came up out of the river 7 well favoured (good-looking) kine (cows) and fatfleshed (fat). And they fed in a meadow.
And look, 7 other kine (cows) came up after them out of the river, ill favoured (ugly) and leanfleshed (thin). And they stood by the other kine (cows) on the brink (edge) of the river.
And the ill favoured (ugly) and leanfleshed (thin) kine (cows) ate up the 7 well favoured (good-looking) and fat kine (cows). So Pharaoh awoke.
And Pharaoh slept and dreamed the 2nd time. And look, 7 ears of corn (heads of grain) came up on one stalk, rank (full) and good.
And look, 7 thin ears (heads of grain) and blasted (dried up) with the east wind sprung up after them.
And the 7 thin ears (heads of grain) devoured (ate up) the 7 rank (full) and full ears (heads of grain). And Pharaoh awoke, and look, it was a dream.

And it came to pass in the morning that Pharaoh's spirit was troubled. And he sent and called for all the magicians of Egypt, and all the wise men of it. And Pharaoh told them his dream, but there was none that could interpret (tell the meaning of) them to Pharaoh.
Then the chief butler (cupbearer) spoke to Pharaoh, saying: I do remember my faults this day.
Pharaoh was wroth (very angry) with his servants, and put me in ward (under guard) in the captain of the guard's house, both me and the chief baker.
And we dreamed a dream in one night, I and he. We dreamed each man according to the interpretation (meaning) of his dream.

And there was there with us a young man, a Hebrew, servant to the captain of the guard. And we told him, and he interpreted (told the meaning of) to us our dreams. To each man according to his dream he did interpret (tell the meaning of).
And it came to pass, as he interpreted (told the meaning of) to us, so it was. Me Pharaoh restored to my office (job), and the baker he hanged.
Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily (quickly) out of the dungeon. And Joseph shaved himself, and changed his raiment (clothes), and came in to Pharaoh.

And Pharaoh said to Joseph: I have dreamed a dream, and there is none that can interpret (tell the meaning of) it. And I have heard it said of you that you can understand a dream to interpret (tell the meaning of) it.
And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying: It is not in me. God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph: In my dream, look, I stood on the bank of the river.
And look, there came up out of the river 7 kine (cows), fatfleshed (fat) and well favoured (good-looking). And they fed in a meadow.
And look, 7 other kine (cows) came up after them, poor and very ill favoured (ugly) and leanfleshed (thin), such as I never saw in all the land of Egypt for badness.
And the lean and the ill favoured (ugly) kine (cows) ate up the first 7 fat kine (cows).
And when they had eaten them up, it could not be known that they had eaten them. But they were still ill favoured (ugly), as at the beginning. So I awoke.
And I saw in my dream, and look, 7 ears (heads of grain) came up in one stalk, full and good.
And look, 7 ears (heads of grain), withered, thin, and blasted (dried up) with the east wind, sprung up after them.
And the thin ears (heads of grain) devoured (ate up) the 7 good ears (heads of grain). And I told this to the magicians, but there was none that could declare (explain) it to me.
And Joseph said to Pharaoh: The dream of Pharaoh is one. God has shown Pharaoh what He is about to do.
The 7 good kine (cows) are 7 years, and the 7 good ears (heads of grain) are 7 years. The dream is one.

And the 7 thin and ill favoured (ugly) kine (cows) that came up after them are 7 years. And the 7 empty ears (heads of grain) blasted (dried up) with the east wind shall be 7 years of famine (time of no food).
This is the thing which I have spoken to Pharaoh: what God is about to do He shows to Pharaoh.
Look, there come 7 years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt.
And there shall arise after them 7 years of famine (time of no food). And all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt, and the famine (time of no food) shall consume (eat up) the land.
And the plenty shall not be known in the land because of that famine (time of no food) following, for it shall be very grievous (very bad).
And because the dream was doubled to Pharaoh twice, it is because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.
Now then, let Pharaoh look out a man discreet (wise in judgment) and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt.
Let Pharaoh do this, and let him appoint officers over the land, and take up the 5th part of the land of Egypt in the 7 plenteous (plentiful) years.
And let them gather all the food of those good years that come, and lay up corn (grain) under the hand of Pharaoh. And let them keep food in the cities.

And that food shall be for store to the land against the 7 years of famine (time of no food), which shall be in the land of Egypt, so that the land does not perish (die) through the famine (time of no food).
And the thing was good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.
And Pharaoh said to his servants: Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the Spirit of God is?
And Pharaoh said to Joseph: Since God has shown you all this, there is none so discreet (wise in judgment) and wise as you are.
You shall be over my house, and according to your word all my people shall be ruled. Only in the throne will I be greater than you.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph: See, I have set you over all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh took off his ring from his hand, and put it on Joseph's hand, and arrayed (dressed) him in vestures (clothes) of fine linen, and put a gold chain around his neck.
And Pharaoh made him to ride in the 2nd chariot which he had. And they cried before him: Bow the knee. And Pharaoh made him ruler over all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph: I am Pharaoh, and without you no man shall lift up his hand or foot in all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh called Joseph's name Zaphnathpaaneah. And he gave him as wife Asenath the daughter of Potipherah priest of On. And Joseph went out over all the land of Egypt.
And Joseph was 30 years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went throughout all the land of Egypt.
And in the 7 plenteous (plentiful) years the earth brought out by handfuls.
And Joseph gathered up all the food of the 7 years, which were in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities. The food of the field, which was around every city, he laid up in the same.
And Joseph gathered corn (grain) as the sand of the sea, very much, until he left numbering (stopped counting), for it was without number.
And to Joseph were born 2 sons before the years of famine (time of no food) came, which Asenath the daughter of Potipherah priest of On bore to him.
And Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh (making forget). For God, he said, has made me forget all my toil (hard work), and all my father's house.
And the name of the 2nd he called Ephraim (fruitful). For God has caused me to be fruitful (grow and do well) in the land of my affliction (suffering).
And the 7 years of plenteousness (plenty), that was in the land of Egypt, were ended.
And the 7 years of dearth (time of no food) began to come, as Joseph had said. And the dearth (time of no food) was in all lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.
And when all the land of Egypt was famished (starving), the people cried to Pharaoh for bread. And Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians: Go to Joseph. What he says to you, do.

And the famine (time of no food) was over all the face of the earth. And Joseph opened all the storehouses, and sold to the Egyptians. And the famine (time of no food) waxed (grew) sore (very bad) in the land of Egypt.
And all countries came into Egypt to Joseph to buy corn (grain), because the famine (time of no food) was so sore (very bad) in all lands.

41.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V45 keeps the KJV's name Zaphnathpaaneah. V54 keeps the KJV's dearth (time of no food). Kept hidden (needs-review) until the editor reviews it.

verses.text: Now when Jacob saw that there was corn (grain) in Egypt, Jacob said to his sons: Why do you look one on another?
And Jacob said: Look, I have heard that there is corn (grain) in Egypt. Get down there, and buy for us from there, so that we may live, and not die.
And Joseph's 10 brethren (brothers) went down to buy corn (grain) in Egypt.
But Benjamin, Joseph's brother, Jacob did not send with his brethren (brothers). For Jacob said: Peradventure (maybe) mischief (harm) might befall (happen to) him.
And the sons of Israel came to buy corn (grain) among those that came, for the famine (time of no food) was in the land of Canaan.

And Joseph was the governor over the land, and he was the one that sold to all the people of the land. And Joseph's brethren (brothers) came, and bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth.

And Joseph saw his brethren (brothers), and he knew them, but made himself strange (acted like a stranger) to them, and spoke roughly to them. And he said to them: Where do you come from? And they said: From the land of Canaan to buy food.
And Joseph knew his brethren (brothers), but they did not know him.
And Joseph remembered the dreams which he dreamed of them, and said to them: You are spies. You have come to see the nakedness (weak places) of the land.
And they said to him: No, my lord, but your servants have come to buy food.
We are all one man's sons. We are true men. Your servants are no spies.
And Joseph said to them: No, but you have come to see the nakedness (weak places) of the land.
And they said: Your servants are 12 brethren (brothers), the sons of one man in the land of Canaan. And look, the youngest is this day with our father, and one is not (is gone).
And Joseph said to them: That is what I spoke to you, saying: You are spies.
By this you shall be proved (tested): by the life of Pharaoh you shall not go out from here, except your youngest brother comes here.

Send one of you, and let him fetch your brother, and you shall be kept in prison, so that your words may be proved, whether there is any truth in you. Or else by the life of Pharaoh surely you are spies.
And Joseph put them all together into ward (under guard) 3 days.
And Joseph said to them the 3rd day: Do this, and live, for I fear God.
If you are true men, let one of your brethren (brothers) be bound in the house of your prison. Go, carry corn (grain) for the famine (time of no food) of your houses.
But bring your youngest brother to me. So your words shall be verified (proved true), and you shall not die. And they did so.

And they said one to another: We are verily (truly) guilty about our brother, in that we saw the anguish (deep pain) of his soul, when he besought (begged) us, and we would not hear. So this trouble has come on us.
And Reuben answered them, saying: Did I not speak to you, saying: Do not sin against the child, and you would not hear? So look, also his blood is required (must be paid for).
And they did not know that Joseph understood them, for he spoke to them by an interpreter (one who changes words into another language).
And Joseph turned himself away from them, and wept. And he returned to them again, and communed (talked) with them, and took from them Simeon, and bound him before their eyes.
Then Joseph commanded to fill their sacks with corn (grain), and to restore every man's money into his sack, and to give them provision (food) for the way. And so he did to them.
And they laded (loaded) their asses (donkeys) with the corn (grain), and departed from there.
And as one of them opened his sack to give his ass (donkey) provender (animal food) in the inn, he espied (saw) his money. For look, it was in his sack's mouth.

And he said to his brethren (brothers): My money is restored. And look, it is even in my sack. And their heart failed them, and they were afraid, saying one to another: What is this that God has done to us?
And they came to Jacob their father to the land of Canaan, and told him all that befell (happened) to them, saying:
The man, who is the lord of the land, spoke roughly to us, and took us for spies of the country.
And we said to him: We are true men. We are no spies.
We are 12 brethren (brothers), sons of our father. One is not, and the youngest is this day with our father in the land of Canaan.

And the man, the lord of the country, said to us: By this I shall know that you are true men: leave one of your brethren (brothers) here with me, and take food for the famine (time of no food) of your households, and be gone.
And bring your youngest brother to me. Then I shall know that you are no spies, but that you are true men. So I will deliver to you your brother, and you shall traffick (trade) in the land.
And it came to pass as they emptied their sacks that, look, every man's bundle of money was in his sack. And when both they and their father saw the bundles of money, they were afraid.
And Jacob their father said to them: You have bereaved (robbed) me of my children. Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and you will take Benjamin away. All these things are against me.
And Reuben spoke to his father, saying: Slay my 2 sons, if I do not bring Benjamin to you. Deliver him into my hand, and I will bring him to you again.

And Jacob said: My son shall not go down with you, for his brother is dead, and he is left alone. If mischief (harm) befalls (happens to) him by the way in which you go, then you shall bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave.

42.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V21 uses trouble for the KJV's distress (house rule). V38 keeps the KJV's grave.

verses.text: And the famine (time of no food) was sore (very bad) in the land.
And it came to pass, when they had eaten up the corn (grain) which they had brought out of Egypt, their father said to them: Go again, buy us a little food.
And Judah spoke to him, saying: The man did solemnly protest (strongly warn) to us, saying: You shall not see my face, except your brother is with you.
If you will send our brother with us, we will go down and buy you food.
But if you will not send him, we will not go down. For the man said to us: You shall not see my face, except your brother is with you.
And Israel said: Why did you deal so ill (badly) with me, as to tell the man whether you had yet a brother?

And they said: The man asked us straitly (closely) about our state, and about our kindred, saying: Is your father yet alive? Have you another brother? And we told him according to the tenor (meaning) of these words. Could we certainly know that he would say: Bring your brother down?
And Judah said to Israel his father: Send the lad (boy) with me, and we will arise and go, so that we may live, and not die, both we, and you, and also our little ones.
I will be surety (guarantee) for him. Of my hand you shall require him. If I do not bring him to you, and set him before you, then let me bear the blame forever.
For except we had lingered, surely now we would have returned this 2nd time.

And their father Israel said to them: If it must be so now, do this: take of the best fruits in the land in your vessels (containers), and carry down the man a present: a little balm (healing oil), and a little honey, spices, and myrrh (sweet-smelling gum), nuts, and almonds.
And take double money in your hand. And the money that was brought again in the mouth of your sacks, carry it again in your hand. Peradventure (maybe) it was an oversight (mistake).
Take also your brother, and arise, go again to the man.
And God Almighty give you mercy before the man, so that he may send away your other brother, and Benjamin. If I am bereaved (robbed) of my children, I am bereaved.
And the men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin. And they rose up, and went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
And when Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the ruler of his house: Bring these men home, and slay (kill an animal), and make ready. For these men shall dine (eat) with me at noon.
And the man did as Joseph bade (told him). And the man brought the men into Joseph's house.

And the men were afraid, because they were brought into Joseph's house. And they said: Because of the money that was returned in our sacks at the first time we are brought in, so that he may seek occasion (a reason) against us, and fall on us, and take us for bondmen (slaves), and our asses (donkeys).
And they came near to the steward (manager) of Joseph's house, and they communed (talked) with him at the door of the house,
And said: O sir, we came indeed down at the first time to buy food.
And it came to pass, when we came to the inn, that we opened our sacks, and look, every man's money was in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight. And we have brought it again in our hand.
And other money we have brought down in our hands to buy food. We cannot tell who put our money in our sacks.
And the steward (manager) said: Peace be to you. Fear not. Your God, and the God of your father, has given you treasure in your sacks. I had your money. And he brought Simeon out to them.
And the man brought the men into Joseph's house, and gave them water, and they washed their feet. And he gave their asses (donkeys) provender (animal food).
And they made ready the present for when Joseph came at noon, for they heard that they should eat bread there.
And when Joseph came home, they brought him the present which was in their hand into the house, and bowed themselves to him to the earth.
And Joseph asked them about their welfare (how they were), and said: Is your father well, the old man of whom you spoke? Is he yet alive?
And they answered: Your servant our father is in good health. He is yet alive. And they bowed down their heads, and made obeisance (bowed low).
And Joseph lifted up his eyes, and saw his brother Benjamin, his mother's son, and said: Is this your younger brother, of whom you spoke to me? And Joseph said: God be gracious to you, my son.
And Joseph made haste, for his bowels did yearn (his deep love was stirred) for his brother. And he looked for a place to weep. And he entered into his chamber (room), and wept there.
And Joseph washed his face, and went out, and refrained (held back) himself, and said: Set on bread.

And they set food for Joseph by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians, which ate with him, by themselves. Because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination (a hateful thing) to the Egyptians.
And they sat before Joseph, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth. And the men marvelled (were amazed) one at another.
And Joseph took and sent messes (portions of food) to them from before him. But Benjamin's mess was 5 times as much as any of theirs. And they drank, and were merry with him.

43.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V34 was missing from the site and is restored from the KJV. V30 keeps the KJV's his bowels did yearn (his deep love was stirred).

verses.text: And Joseph commanded the steward (manager) of his house, saying: Fill the men's sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put every man's money in his sack's mouth.
And put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack's mouth of the youngest, and his corn (grain) money. And the steward (manager) did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.
As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away, they and their asses (donkeys).

And when they had gone out of the city, and were not yet far off, Joseph said to his steward (manager): Up, follow after the men. And when you overtake them, say to them: Why have you rewarded evil for good?
Is not this the cup in which my lord drinks, and by which indeed he divines (tells secret things)? You have done evil in so doing.
And the steward (manager) overtook them, and he spoke to them these same words.
And they said to him: Why does my lord say these words? God forbid that your servants should do such a thing.
Look, the money, which we found in our sacks' mouths, we brought again to you out of the land of Canaan. How then should we steal out of your lord's house silver or gold?
With whomever of your servants it is found, let him die, and we also will be my lord's bondmen (slaves).
And the steward (manager) said: Now also let it be according to your words. He with whom it is found shall be my servant, and you shall be blameless.
Then they speedily took down every man his sack to the ground, and opened every man his sack.
And the steward (manager) searched, and began at the eldest, and left at the youngest. And the cup was found in Benjamin's sack.
Then they rent (tore) their clothes, and laded (loaded) every man his ass (donkey), and returned to the city.
And Judah and his brethren (brothers) came to Joseph's house, for he was yet there. And they fell before him on the ground.
And Joseph said to them: What deed is this that you have done? Do you not wot (know) that such a man as I can certainly divine (tell secret things)?

And Judah said: What shall we say to my lord? What shall we speak? Or how shall we clear ourselves? God has found out the iniquity (sin) of your servants. Look, we are my lord's servants, both we, and he also with whom the cup is found.
And Joseph said: God forbid that I should do so. But the man in whose hand the cup is found, he shall be my servant. And as for you, get up in peace to your father.
Then Judah came near to him, and said: Oh my lord, let your servant, I pray you, speak a word in my lord's ears, and let not your anger burn against your servant. For you are even as Pharaoh.
My lord asked his servants, saying: Have you a father, or a brother?
And we said to my lord: We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, a little one. And his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother, and his father loves him.
And you said to your servants: Bring him down to me, so that I may set my eyes on him.
And we said to my lord: The lad (boy) cannot leave his father. For if he should leave his father, his father would die.
And you said to your servants: Except your youngest brother comes down with you, you shall see my face no more.
And it came to pass when we came up to your servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.
And our father said: Go again, and buy us a little food.
And we said: We cannot go down. If our youngest brother is with us, then we will go down. For we may not see the man's face, except our youngest brother is with us.
And your servant my father said to us: You know that my wife bore me 2 sons.
And the one went out from me, and I said: Surely he is torn in pieces. And I have not seen him since.
And if you take this one also from me, and mischief (harm) befalls (happens to) him, you shall bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave.
Now then when I come to your servant my father, and the lad (boy) is not with us, since his life is bound up in the lad's (boy's) life,
It shall come to pass, when he sees that the lad (boy) is not with us, that he will die. And your servants shall bring down the gray hairs of your servant our father with sorrow to the grave.
For your servant became surety (guarantee) for the lad (boy) to my father, saying: If I do not bring him to you, then I shall bear the blame to my father forever.
Now then, I pray you, let your servant abide (stay) instead of the lad (boy) a bondman (slave) to my lord. And let the lad (boy) go up with his brethren (brothers).
For how shall I go up to my father, and the lad (boy) is not with me? Or else I will see the evil that shall come on my father.

44.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V5 and v15 keep the KJV's divine (tell secret things), as Joseph's steward and Joseph say it.

verses.text: Then Joseph could not refrain (hold back) himself before all them that stood by him. And he cried: Make every man go out from me. And there stood no man with him, while Joseph made himself known to his brethren (brothers).
And Joseph wept aloud. And the Egyptians and the house of Pharaoh heard.
And Joseph said to his brethren (brothers): I am Joseph. Does my father yet live? And his brethren (brothers) could not answer him, for they were troubled at his presence.
And Joseph said to his brethren (brothers): Come near to me, I pray you. And they came near. And he said: I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
Now then do not be grieved (sad), nor angry with yourselves, that you sold me here. For God did send me before you to preserve (save) life.
For these 2 years the famine (time of no food) has been in the land. And yet there are 5 years, in which there shall be neither earing (plowing) nor harvest.
And God sent me before you to preserve you a posterity (a family line) in the earth, and to save your lives by a great deliverance (rescue).
So now it was not you that sent me here, but God. And He has made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and a ruler throughout all the land of Egypt.
Hurry, and go up to my father, and say to him: Your son Joseph says this: God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me. Do not tarry (stay).
And you shall dwell (live) in the land of Goshen, and you shall be near to me, you, and your children, and your children's children, and your flocks, and your herds, and all that you have.
And there I will nourish (feed) you, for yet there are 5 years of famine (time of no food), so that you, and your household, and all that you have, do not come to poverty.
And look, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaks to you.
And you shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that you have seen. And you shall hurry and bring down my father here.
And Joseph fell on his brother Benjamin's neck, and wept. And Benjamin wept on his neck.
Also Joseph kissed all his brethren (brothers), and wept on them. And after that his brethren (brothers) talked with him.
And the fame (news) of it was heard in Pharaoh's house, saying: Joseph's brethren (brothers) have come. And it pleased Pharaoh well, and his servants.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph: Say to your brethren (brothers): Do this: lade (load) your beasts, and go, get to the land of Canaan.
And take your father and your households, and come to me. And I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and you shall eat the fat (best part) of the land.
Now you are commanded, do this: take wagons out of the land of Egypt for your little ones, and for your wives, and bring your father, and come.
Also regard not (do not worry about) your stuff, for the good of all the land of Egypt is yours.
And the children of Israel did so. And Joseph gave them wagons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh, and gave them provision (food) for the way.
To all of them Joseph gave each man changes of raiment (clothes). But to Benjamin he gave 300 pieces of silver, and 5 changes of raiment (clothes).

And to his father he sent in this way: 10 asses (donkeys) laden (loaded) with the good things of Egypt, and 10 she asses (female donkeys) laden (loaded) with corn (grain) and bread and meat (food) for his father by the way.
So Joseph sent his brethren (brothers) away, and they departed. And he said to them: See that you do not fall out (argue) by the way.
And they went up out of Egypt, and came into the land of Canaan to Jacob their father,
And told him, saying: Joseph is yet alive, and he is governor over all the land of Egypt. And Jacob's heart fainted (went weak), for he did not believe them.
And they told him all the words of Joseph, which he had said to them. And when Jacob saw the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob their father revived (came back to life).
And Israel said: It is enough. Joseph my son is yet alive. I will go and see him before I die.

45.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V6 keeps the KJV's earing (plowing). V8 keeps the KJV's a father to Pharaoh.

verses.text: And Israel took his journey with all that he had, and came to Beersheba, and offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.
And God spoke to Israel in the visions of the night, and said: Jacob, Jacob. And he said: Here am I.
And He said: I am God, the God of your father. Fear not to go down into Egypt, for I will there make of you a great nation.
I will go down with you into Egypt, and I will also surely bring you up again. And Joseph shall put his hand on your eyes.
And Jacob rose up from Beersheba. And the sons of Israel carried Jacob their father, and their little ones, and their wives, in the wagons which Pharaoh had sent to carry him.
And they took their cattle (farm animals), and their goods, which they had gotten in the land of Canaan, and came into Egypt, Jacob, and all his seed (children) with him:
His sons, and his sons' sons with him, his daughters, and his sons' daughters, and all his seed (children) he brought with him into Egypt.
And these are the names of the children of Israel, which came into Egypt, Jacob and his sons: Reuben, Jacob's firstborn.
And the sons of Reuben: Hanoch, and Phallu, and Hezron, and Carmi.
And the sons of Simeon: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanitish (Canaanite) woman.
And the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
And the sons of Judah: Er, and Onan, and Shelah, and Pharez, and Zarah. But Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. And the sons of Pharez were Hezron and Hamul.
And the sons of Issachar: Tola, and Phuvah, and Job, and Shimron.
And the sons of Zebulun: Sered, and Elon, and Jahleel.
These are the sons of Leah, which she bore to Jacob in Padanaram, with his daughter Dinah. All the souls (people) of his sons and his daughters were 33.
And the sons of Gad: Ziphion, and Haggi, Shuni, and Ezbon, Eri, and Arodi, and Areli.
And the sons of Asher: Jimnah, and Ishuah, and Isui, and Beriah, and Serah their sister. And the sons of Beriah: Heber, and Malchiel.
These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah his daughter. And these she bore to Jacob, even 16 souls (people).
The sons of Rachel Jacob's wife: Joseph, and Benjamin.
And to Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, which Asenath the daughter of Potipherah priest of On bore to him.
And the sons of Benjamin were Belah, and Becher, and Ashbel, Gera, and Naaman, Ehi, and Rosh, Muppim, and Huppim, and Ard.
These are the sons of Rachel, which were born to Jacob. All the souls (people) were 14.
And the sons of Dan: Hushim.
And the sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, and Guni, and Jezer, and Shillem.
These are the sons of Bilhah, which Laban gave to Rachel his daughter, and she bore these to Jacob. All the souls (people) were 7.
All the souls (people) that came with Jacob into Egypt, which came out of his loins (body), besides Jacob's sons' wives, all the souls (people) were 66.
And the sons of Joseph, which were born to him in Egypt, were 2 souls (people). All the souls (people) of the house of Jacob, which came into Egypt, were 70.
And he sent Judah before him to Joseph, to direct his face to Goshen (to show the way to Goshen). And they came into the land of Goshen.
And Joseph made ready his chariot, and went up to meet Israel his father, to Goshen, and presented himself to him. And he fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.
And Israel said to Joseph: Now let me die, since I have seen your face, because you are yet alive.

And Joseph said to his brethren (brothers), and to his father's house: I will go up, and show Pharaoh, and say to him: My brethren (brothers), and my father's house, which were in the land of Canaan, have come to me.
And the men are shepherds, for their trade has been to feed cattle (farm animals). And they have brought their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have.
And it shall come to pass, when Pharaoh shall call you, and shall say: What is your occupation (work)?

That you shall say: Your servants' trade has been about cattle (farm animals) from our youth even until now, both we, and also our fathers. Say this so that you may dwell (live) in the land of Goshen, for every shepherd is an abomination (a hateful thing) to the Egyptians.

46.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. Names are spelled as the KJV has them (Phallu, Carmi, Jachin, Pharez, Zarah, Phuvah, Job, Ziphion, Jimnah, Ishuah, Isui, Malchiel, Belah, Becher, Jahzeel). V34 keeps the KJV's abomination (a hateful thing).

verses.text: Then Joseph came and told Pharaoh, and said: My father and my brethren (brothers), and their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have, have come out of the land of Canaan. And look, they are in the land of Goshen.
And he took some of his brethren (brothers), even 5 men, and presented them to Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh said to his brethren (brothers): What is your occupation (work)? And they said to Pharaoh: Your servants are shepherds, both we, and also our fathers.

They said also to Pharaoh: We have come to sojourn (stay for a while) in the land, for your servants have no pasture (grassland) for their flocks, for the famine (time of no food) is sore (very bad) in the land of Canaan. Now then, we pray you, let your servants dwell (live) in the land of Goshen.
And Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, saying: Your father and your brethren (brothers) have come to you.

The land of Egypt is before you. In the best of the land make your father and brethren (brothers) to dwell (live). In the land of Goshen let them dwell (live). And if you know any men of activity (able men) among them, then make them rulers over my cattle (farm animals).
And Joseph brought in Jacob his father, and set him before Pharaoh. And Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh said to Jacob: How old are you?

And Jacob said to Pharaoh: The days of the years of my pilgrimage (journey through life) are 130 years. Few and evil have the days of the years of my life been, and have not attained (reached) to the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their pilgrimage (journey through life).
And Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from before Pharaoh.
And Joseph placed his father and his brethren (brothers), and gave them a possession (land to own) in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
And Joseph nourished (fed) his father, and his brethren (brothers), and all his father's household, with bread, according to their families.

And there was no bread in all the land, for the famine (time of no food) was very sore (very bad), so that the land of Egypt and all the land of Canaan fainted (grew weak) because of the famine (time of no food).
And Joseph gathered up all the money that was found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the corn (grain) which they bought. And Joseph brought the money into Pharaoh's house.

And when money failed (ran out) in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came to Joseph, and said: Give us bread. For why should we die in your presence? For the money fails (has run out).
And Joseph said: Give your cattle (farm animals), and I will give you food for your cattle (farm animals), if money fails (has run out).

And they brought their cattle (farm animals) to Joseph. And Joseph gave them bread in exchange for horses, and for the flocks, and for the cattle (farm animals) of the herds, and for the asses (donkeys). And he fed them with bread for all their cattle (farm animals) for that year.

When that year was ended, they came to him the 2nd year, and said to him: We will not hide it from my lord, how our money is spent. My lord also has our herds of cattle (farm animals). There is not anything left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies, and our lands.

Why shall we die before your eyes, both we and our land? Buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants to Pharaoh. And give us seed, so that we may live, and not die, so that the land is not desolate (empty and ruined).

And Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh, for the Egyptians sold every man his field, because the famine (time of no food) prevailed (was too strong) over them. So the land became Pharaoh's.
And as for the people, he removed them to cities from one end of the borders of Egypt even to the other end of it.

Only the land of the priests he did not buy, for the priests had a portion (share) given to them by Pharaoh, and did eat their portion (share) which Pharaoh gave them. So they did not sell their lands.
Then Joseph said to the people: Look, I have bought you this day and your land for Pharaoh. Look, here is seed for you, and you shall sow (plant) the land.

And it shall come to pass in the increase (harvest), that you shall give the 5th part to Pharaoh, and 4 parts shall be your own, for seed of the field, and for your food, and for them of your households, and for food for your little ones.
And they said: You have saved our lives. Let us find grace (favor) in the sight of my lord, and we will be Pharaoh's servants.
And Joseph made it a law over the land of Egypt to this day, that Pharaoh should have the 5th part, except the land of the priests only, which did not become Pharaoh's.
And Israel dwelt (lived) in the land of Egypt, in the country of Goshen. And they had possessions (land they owned) there, and grew, and multiplied exceedingly (very much).
And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt 17 years. So the whole age of Jacob was 147 years.

And the time drew near that Israel must die. And he called his son Joseph, and said to him: If now I have found grace (favor) in your sight, put, I pray you, your hand under my thigh, and deal kindly and truly with me. Do not bury me, I pray you, in Egypt.
But I will lie with my fathers, and you shall carry me out of Egypt, and bury me in their buryingplace (grave). And Joseph said: I will do as you have said.
And Israel said: Swear (make a promise before God) to me. And Joseph swore to him. And Israel bowed himself on the bed's head.

47.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V9 keeps the KJV's pilgrimage (journey through life). V31 keeps the KJV's Israel bowed himself on the bed's head.

verses.text: And it came to pass after these things, that one told Joseph: Look, your father is sick. And he took with him his 2 sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
And one told Jacob, and said: Look, your son Joseph comes to you. And Israel strengthened himself, and sat on the bed.
And Jacob said to Joseph: God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, and blessed me,

And said to me: Look, I will make you fruitful (have many children), and multiply you, and I will make of you a multitude (great crowd) of people. And I will give this land to your seed (children) after you for an everlasting possession (land to own forever).
And now your 2 sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, which were born to you in the land of Egypt before I came to you into Egypt, are mine. As Reuben and Simeon, they shall be mine.
And your issue (children), which you beget (become the father of) after them, shall be yours, and shall be called after the name of their brethren (brothers) in their inheritance.

And as for me, when I came from Padan, Rachel died by me in the land of Canaan on the way, when there was yet but a little way to come to Ephrath. And I buried her there on the way of Ephrath. The same is Bethlehem.
And Israel beheld (saw) Joseph's sons, and said: Who are these?
And Joseph said to his father: They are my sons, whom God has given me in this place. And Israel said: Bring them, I pray you, to me, and I will bless them.
Now the eyes of Israel were dim (weak) for age, so that he could not see. And Joseph brought them near to him. And he kissed them, and embraced (hugged) them.
And Israel said to Joseph: I had not thought to see your face. And look, God has shown me also your seed (children).
And Joseph brought them out from between his knees, and he bowed himself with his face to the earth.
And Joseph took them both, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel's left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel's right hand, and brought them near to him.

And Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it on Ephraim's head, who was the younger, and his left hand on Manasseh's head, guiding his hands wittingly (on purpose), for Manasseh was the firstborn.
And he blessed Joseph, and said: God, before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac did walk, the God which fed me all my life long to this day,

The Angel which redeemed (saved) me from all evil, bless the lads (boys). And let my name be named on them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac. And let them grow into a multitude (great crowd) in the middle of the earth.
And when Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand on the head of Ephraim, it displeased (upset) him. And he held up his father's hand, to remove it from Ephraim's head to Manasseh's head.
And Joseph said to his father: Not so, my father, for this is the firstborn. Put your right hand on his head.

And his father refused, and said: I know it, my son, I know it. He also shall become a people, and he also shall be great. But truly his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed (children) shall become a multitude (great crowd) of nations.
And he blessed them that day, saying: In you shall Israel bless, saying: God make you as Ephraim and as Manasseh. And he set Ephraim before Manasseh.
And Israel said to Joseph: Look, I die. But God shall be with you, and bring you again to the land of your fathers.
Also I have given to you one portion (share) above your brethren (brothers), which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.

48.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V16 keeps the KJV's capital Angel which redeemed (saved) me, because Jacob speaks of God Himself. V22 keeps the KJV's one portion (one share) above your brethren.

verses.text: And Jacob called to his sons, and said: Gather yourselves together, so that I may tell you that which shall befall (happen to) you in the last days.
Gather yourselves together, and hear, you sons of Jacob, and hearken (listen) to Israel your father.
Reuben, you are my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength, the excellency (best) of dignity (honor), and the excellency (best) of power.
Unstable as water, you shall not excel (be the best), because you went up to your father's bed. Then you defiled (made unclean) it. He went up to my couch (bed).
Simeon and Levi are brethren (brothers). Instruments (tools) of cruelty are in their habitations (homes).

O my soul, do not come into their secret. To their assembly (meeting), my honor, do not be united (joined). For in their anger they slew (killed) a man, and in their selfwill (stubbornness) they digged down a wall.
Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce, and their wrath (great anger), for it was cruel. I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel.
Judah, you are he whom your brethren (brothers) shall praise. Your hand shall be in the neck of your enemies. Your father's children shall bow down before you.
Judah is a lion's whelp (young lion). From the prey, my son, you have gone up. He stooped down, he couched (lay down) as a lion, and as an old lion. Who shall rouse (wake) him up?
The sceptre (king's rod) shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh (the Messiah) comes. And to Him shall the gathering of the people be.
Binding His foal (young donkey) to the vine, and His ass's colt (young donkey) to the choice (best) vine, He washed His garments (clothes) in wine, and His clothes in the blood of grapes.
His eyes shall be red with wine, and His teeth white with milk.
Zebulun shall dwell (live) at the haven (harbor) of the sea. And he shall be for a haven (harbor) of ships, and his border shall be to Zidon.
Issachar is a strong ass (donkey) couching (lying) down between 2 burdens (loads).
And he saw that rest was good, and the land that it was pleasant, and bowed his shoulder to bear, and became a servant to tribute (forced work).
Dan shall judge his people, as one of the tribes of Israel.
Dan shall be a serpent (snake) by the way, an adder (poisonous snake) in the path, that bites the horse's heels, so that his rider shall fall backward.
I have waited for Your salvation, O LORD.
Gad, a troop (band of raiders) shall overcome him, but he shall overcome at the last.
Out of Asher his bread shall be fat (rich), and he shall yield royal dainties (food fit for a king).
Naphtali is a hind (female deer) let loose. He gives goodly (beautiful) words.
Joseph is a fruitful (fruit-bearing) bough (branch), even a fruitful (fruit-bearing) bough (branch) by a well, whose branches run over the wall.
The archers have sorely (badly) grieved (hurt) him, and shot at him, and hated him.
But his bow abode (stayed) in strength, and the arms of his hands were made strong by the hands of the mighty God of Jacob. (From there is the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel.)

Even by the God of your father, who shall help you, and by the Almighty, who shall bless you with blessings of heaven above, blessings of the deep that lies under, blessings of the breasts, and of the womb.

The blessings of your father have prevailed (been greater) above the blessings of my progenitors (forefathers) to the utmost bound (farthest edge) of the everlasting hills. They shall be on the head of Joseph, and on the crown of the head of him that was separate from his brethren (brothers).
Benjamin shall ravin (tear his prey) as a wolf. In the morning he shall devour (eat up) the prey, and at night he shall divide the spoil (things taken in war).
All these are the 12 tribes of Israel. And this is what their father spoke to them, and blessed them. Every one according to his blessing he blessed them.
And he charged (commanded) them, and said to them: I am to be gathered to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,

In the cave that is in the field of Machpelah, which is before Mamre, in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought with the field of Ephron the Hittite for a possession (land to own) of a buryingplace (grave).
There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife. There they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife. And there I buried Leah.
The purchase of the field and of the cave that is in it was from the children of Heth.
And when Jacob had made an end of commanding his sons, he gathered up his feet into the bed, and yielded up the ghost (died), and was gathered to his people.

49.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. The earlier text added the name Jesus in v10-12, which the KJV does not have there. V10 now keeps the KJV's until Shiloh come, with Shiloh (the Messiah) explained, and v10-12 capitalize Him and His for Shiloh. V24 capitalizes the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel. V18 keeps the KJV's O LORD.

verses.text: And Joseph fell on his father's face, and wept on him, and kissed him.
And Joseph commanded his servants the physicians (doctors) to embalm (prepare the body of) his father. And the physicians (doctors) embalmed (prepared the body of) Israel.
And 40 days were fulfilled (completed) for him, for so are fulfilled (completed) the days of those which are embalmed (prepared for burial). And the Egyptians mourned for him 70 days.
And when the days of his mourning were past, Joseph spoke to the house of Pharaoh, saying: If now I have found grace (favor) in your eyes, speak, I pray you, in the ears of Pharaoh, saying:

My father made me swear (make a promise before God), saying: Look, I die. In my grave which I have digged for me in the land of Canaan, there you shall bury me. Now then let me go up, I pray you, and bury my father, and I will come again.
And Pharaoh said: Go up, and bury your father, as he made you swear (make a promise before God).
And Joseph went up to bury his father. And with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders (leaders) of his house, and all the elders (leaders) of the land of Egypt,
And all the house of Joseph, and his brethren (brothers), and his father's house. Only their little ones, and their flocks, and their herds, they left in the land of Goshen.
And there went up with him both chariots and horsemen. And it was a very great company (group).

And they came to the threshingfloor (place to separate grain) of Atad, which is beyond Jordan, and there they mourned with a great and very sore (very bitter) lamentation (crying). And he made a mourning for his father 7 days.

And when the inhabitants (people who lived there) of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning in the floor of Atad, they said: This is a grievous (heavy) mourning to the Egyptians. So the name of it was called Abelmizraim (mourning of Egypt), which is beyond Jordan.
And his sons did to him as he commanded them.

For his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought with the field for a possession (land to own) of a buryingplace (grave) from Ephron the Hittite, before Mamre.
And Joseph returned into Egypt, he, and his brethren (brothers), and all that went up with him to bury his father, after he had buried his father.
And when Joseph's brethren (brothers) saw that their father was dead, they said: Joseph will peradventure (maybe) hate us, and will certainly requite (pay back) us all the evil which we did to him.
And they sent a messenger to Joseph, saying: Your father did command before he died, saying:

So shall you say to Joseph: Forgive, I pray you now, the trespass (wrong) of your brethren (brothers), and their sin, for they did to you evil. And now, we pray you, forgive the trespass (wrong) of the servants of the God of your father. And Joseph wept when they spoke to him.
And his brethren (brothers) also went and fell down before his face. And they said: Look, we are your servants.
And Joseph said to them: Fear not. For am I in the place of God?
But as for you, you thought evil against me. But God meant it to good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save many people alive.
Now then do not fear. I will nourish (feed) you, and your little ones. And he comforted them, and spoke kindly to them.
And Joseph dwelt (lived) in Egypt, he, and his father's house. And Joseph lived 110 years.
And Joseph saw Ephraim's children of the 3rd generation. The children also of Machir the son of Manasseh were brought up on Joseph's knees.
And Joseph said to his brethren (brothers): I die. And God will surely visit (come to help) you, and bring you out of this land to the land which He swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
And Joseph took an oath (promise before God) of the children of Israel, saying: God will surely visit (come to help) you, and you shall carry up my bones from here.
So Joseph died, being 110 years old. And they embalmed (prepared the body of) him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.

50.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text followed modern Bibles in places), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.
